If you have never had these costs counted, that is not because you failed a
test. It is because nobody added them up.
Write them down on one sheet of paper before you telephone anybody.
Rent or mortgage. Tax. Insurance.
Heat. Power. Water. Trash. The total on that sheet is the number that matters,
and it is a number most people have never worked out in their lives.
And there is a second half to this that nobody mentions.
If you live in a place where the heating bill triples in January, that January
bill counts. Not an average. Not a guess.
What you actually paid. A person who applies in July and a person who applies
in January can be judged on very different figures, from the same house, on
the same income. Almost nobody is told that either.
Number three. Every limit moved on the first except the one that helps you.
On the first of October almost every figure in this system went up.
That is what the first of October is.
The ceilings moved, the deductions moved, the amounts moved.
One thing did not move, and it is the one you want held still.
Medical costs above thirty five dollars a month come off your total.
Thirty five. That floor has not moved, while everything standing around it
has.
Understand how low thirty five dollars is.
It is not a serious illness. It is not a hospital stay.
It is what you already spend without thinking about it.
The pills on repeat. The trip to the doctor and the trip home.
The dentist. The glasses. The hearing aid batteries.
The things you buy off the shelf every month.
The bandages and the ointment and the pills you take for your knees.
Almost every person over sixty spends more than thirty five dollars a month
on health without ever calling it a medical expense.
It is just what life costs. And every dollar above that first thirty five comes
off the number they judge you on.
There is a second figure here and it is the one that stops people cold.
The amount you are allowed to keep in savings went up to four thousand seven
hundred and fifty dollars.
People believe money in the bank ends it right there.
They have three thousand dollars put aside for a funeral or a roof or a grandchild,
and they think that rules them out before they start.
It does not. And in a good many states that test is not run at all any more,
so the whole worry was never real.
That is the third refusal people hand themselves.
Not the income. Not the housing.
The small amount of money they have been careful enough to save.
Now I want to be straight with you about something, because I am not going
to tell you anything I cannot stand behind.
I cannot tell you your own figures.
Every state runs this differently.
Some states dropped the savings test completely and some did not.
Some count things others ignore.
The numbers I have given you are the federal ones that changed on the first
of October, and your state builds on top of them.
So do not take my word for whether you qualify.
Take my word for this instead.
The person who decides is not you, and the decision you made at your own kitchen
table three years ago was made against numbers that no longer exist.
So. Three things, and what each one does.
They never look at your pay before costs come off.
So the big number on the top line was never the one that counted.
Your housing costs above half your income come off with nothing capping them,
which is true for no other kind of home.
And the medical floor held at thirty five dollars while every other limit rose,
with money in the bank allowed up to nearly five thousand.
None of that is hidden. It is published.
It has been published for years.
It works badly for older people only because every one of those offices is
built to answer a question, and not one of them is built to ask.
One last thing, and hold on to it for the next few weeks.
Nobody legitimate telephones you about this.
If a call offers to check your benefits, or to file for you for a fee, or asks
for your card number to confirm anything, that is a fraud.
Applying is free. The help is free.
The only people who charge you are the ones who should not be calling.
And if somebody in your family was refused this year, do not ask them how much
they earn. Ask them one thing.
What month were you turned down?

title: 7 Things IRS Can’t Take From You — Most Seniors Only Know One

segments.text: There is a line running through your money.
On one side is everything they cannot reach.
On the other is everything they can.
Almost nobody over sixty five knows where that line falls in their own accounts.
They know it in a rough way. They have heard that a pension is safe, that Social
Security is protected. Both of those sentences are half true, and the half
that is missing is the half that costs money.
Here is what is happening while you watch this.
Four hundred and fifty two thousand people who receive a Social Security check
are behind on a student loan.
Collection on those loans has already restarted.
The part that reaches into a monthly check is the part that has not started
yet. When it does, the law allows fifteen per cent of the check to be taken.
It protects the first seven hundred and fifty dollars.
That figure has not been raised since nineteen ninety eight.
There are seven things that cannot be taken from you.
Six of them hold. The seventh is where most people find out they were standing
on the wrong side of the line.
Number one. The retirement plan you got through work has no dollar limit on
it at all. Not a high limit. No limit at all.
That is worth hearing twice, because almost nobody believes it the first time.
If you worked somewhere and paid into a plan through the payroll, that money
sits under a federal rule that says a creditor cannot reach it.
Not a credit card company. Not a hospital.
Not a company that bought an old debt of yours for pennies.
Not a court judgment from a lawsuit.
There is no ceiling written into it.
A person with four hundred thousand dollars in that plan is covered on all
of it, the same as a person with forty thousand.
Understand how unusual that is.
Almost every protection in American law comes with a number attached.
This one does not. And there is a reason so few people know it.
The protection lives in the plan, not in the person.
Nobody writes to tell you about a rule that protects you.
You would only ever learn it from somebody trying to collect, and it is the
last thing they would say out loud.
If you are on the telephone with a
collector and there is money in a work retirement
plan, that money is not theirs to discuss.
It is not an asset they are entitled to discuss.
Number two. The account you opened yourself is a different animal, and this
is where people get hurt. A great many people have both.
A plan from an employer, and an account they opened at a bank or a brokerage
on their own. They think of it as one pot of retirement money.
The law does not.
Here is the split, and it is worth hearing twice.
If the money in your own account came out of an employer plan and was moved
across, it carries the full protection with it.
No limit. It keeps what it had.
If you opened it and paid into it yourself over the years, the protection stops
at about one million seven hundred thousand dollars.
And that is not for each account.
That is for every account of that kind you own, added together.
Now, most people watching this are nowhere near that figure, and there is no
point pretending otherwise. So why does it matter.
It matters because of what it tells you about the second kind of account.
It is protected by a different rule, a weaker one, and one that was written
for a courtroom most people will never see.
Number three. Outside of a bankruptcy court, that second kind of account has
no federal shield at all. That sentence is the one to carry out of this video.
The limit I just described is a bankruptcy rule.
It applies when somebody files.
If you never file, and a creditor simply sues you and wins, that rule is not
in the room. What decides it then is your own state.
And the states are not close to each other.
Some protect that account completely, the same as a work plan.
Some protect a portion. Some protect very little.
A person in one state can be untouchable.
A person two hundred miles away is not, with the same money, in the same kind
of account, at the same bank. There is no letter that tells you which one you
are. There is no notice. The first time most people find out is when somebody
is already trying to collect, which is the worst moment there is to learn it.
So find out now, while nothing is wrong.
Your state legal aid office handles this every day and does it free for people
over sixty. Ask them one question.
In this state, is a retirement account I opened myself protected from a judgment.
That is a five minute call, and the answer changes what happens to that money.
Number four. The money stops being protected the moment it leaves.
Same dollar. Different rules. Sitting in the account it cannot be touched.
Sitting in your checking account it can.
This is the one that catches careful people, and it catches them while they
are doing something sensible. Somebody takes a withdrawal to cover a roof,
or a car, or a medical bill. The money lands in checking and sits there for
three weeks while they arrange the work.
During those three weeks it is ordinary money, with none of the protection
it had on the morning it left.
If there is a judgment against that person, or one arrives during those weeks,
that money is reachable and the money it came from was not.
So the rule is narrow and it is easy.
Do not move money out before you need it.
Move it when the bill is in front of you, not when you are thinking about the
bill. And if somebody has already sued you, or you think they are about to,
do not take a withdrawal at all until you have spoken to somebody.
Taking your own money out of a protected place, in that situation, is the single
most expensive thing you can do by accident.
Number five. There are three doors that open in a plan that is otherwise shut.
I would rather you heard these from me than found them the hard way.
The first is the government collecting tax it says you owe.
A work retirement plan is closed to private creditors and it is not closed
to the tax authority. That is the largest exception and it is the one people
are most surprised by. The second is a court order from a divorce.
If a court divided that plan between two people, that order reaches inside
it. The plan does not overrule the court.
The third is certain criminal penalties.
Narrow, rare, and worth knowing exists.
Everything else stays outside.
A hospital bill, a card, a store account, an old debt sold on, a judgment from
a fall on land that belongs to somebody else.
All outside. So when somebody tells you your retirement money can be taken,
the honest answer is that three specific things can reach it and nothing else
can. Ask which of the three they mean.
Most of the time they cannot answer, because they were repeating something
they heard.
Number six. When one of a married couple goes into care, there is an amount
the one at home is allowed to keep.
This is the item almost nobody knows, and it decides what a widow lives on.
When a husband or a wife goes into a nursing home and the state pays for that
care, the state looks at the money the couple has.
People assume that means everything is counted and everything must be spent.
That is not what the rule says.
The one still living at home keeps a share of what the couple built, plus their
own income, plus the house they live in.
The figures move every year and they differ by state, so naming one would only
be wrong where you live. What I want you to hear is that the amount is not
small, it is not a kindness, and it is not something you have to argue for.
It is written down.
And here is why it matters on a video about what cannot be taken.
Families spend money they were entitled to keep, because somebody at a kitchen
table decided that the rules must require it, and nobody checked.
So before a single dollar is spent down, make one call.
Your state legal aid office, or your area agency on aging.
Ask what the one still at home keeps this year, in this state.
Number seven. Fifteen per cent, and a floor set in nineteen ninety eight.
Everything above is about private creditors.
This one is the government, and it is the reason this video exists now rather
than last year. There are three point two million people aged sixty two and
over carrying federal student loan debt.
Nearly one hundred and forty four billion dollars of it.
Some of it is their own, from going back to study.
A great deal of it is not. It was borrowed for a child or a grandchild, and
the older person signed.
Of those, the number already behind and drawing a Social Security check is
the one from the start of this video.
When a federal student loan is in default, the government can take up to fifteen
per cent of that check before it ever reaches the account.
It does not need to sue. It does not need a judge.
There is no court in it. The protected floor is seven hundred and fifty dollars
a month. Below that they take nothing.
Above it, they can take fifteen per cent.
Sit with the year on that figure.
Nineteen ninety eight.
It has not moved since.
Everything a person buys has moved and that floor has not.
Where it stands right now is the part people are getting wrong.
Collection on these loans restarted this year.
The piece that reaches into Social Security checks was held back in January
and has not switched on yet. A bill
was introduced in August to stop it permanently.
It has not passed.
So the position tonight is that it is paused, not cancelled, and nobody is
going to write and warn you the week before it changes.
One payment sits fully outside all of it.
The payment called, the payment known as SSI cannot be touched for this.
Not at any amount, not by anybody.
And there are three ways out that exist right now, while it is still paused.
Nine payments on time over ten months takes a loan out of default.
A person too ill to work can apply to have the debt wiped out entirely.
And anybody can file a hardship objection before an offset begins.
Every one of those has to be started before the money moves.
Afterwards is a different talk, and a much worse one.
So, seven things, and which side of the line each one sits on.
The plan you got through work is closed to private creditors with no dollar
limit. The one you opened yourself is capped, and only inside a bankruptcy.
Outside a bankruptcy, your state decides it.
Money that leaves the account loses everything the account gave it.
Three doors open in a work plan, and the tax authority is the widest.
When one of a couple goes into care, the other keeps a share, a house and an
income. And a defaulted student loan reaches a Social Security check without
a judge, up to fifteen per cent, above a floor that was set in nineteen ninety
eight.
Six of those protect you. One of them does not.
And the one that does not is the only one moving this month.
Nothing here is advice about you in particular.
States write their own figures, and yours will not be the ones spoken tonight.
One last thing. Nobody legitimate telephones about any of this.
If a call says your retirement account is at risk and there is a fee to protect
it, that is a fraud, every time.
The protection is already yours and it costs nothing.
And if you are helping somebody with a loan they signed for a grandchild, do
not ask them how much it is. Ask them one thing.
Is it in default right now.

title: Every Senior Over 65: The Real Dates This Bill Hits Your Money

segments.text: Every month there is money taken out of your check before you ever see it.
You have never paid it by hand.
It is simply moved.
There is a program that will pay that amount for you.
Not refund it. Pay it, so it stops being taken and your deposit is larger next
month. You may have qualified for years.
You will not be told. A rule was written so the government would find people
like you and sign them up itself.
Somebody switched that rule off.
No letter will reach you, because nobody writes to you about a thing that did
not happen.
That is the sixth of six, and it is the only one that puts money back.
The other five take, and not one of them will arrive with your name on it.
They reach you through your daughter.
Through your doctor. Through a counter at a care home you have never walked
into. You will find out once it has already happened.
Number one. The letter that asks you to prove it again now comes twice a year.
There is a letter that goes out to everybody on Medicaid asking them to show
they still qualify. It used to come once a year.
For adults under sixty five it now has to come every six months, and states
have to have that running by the thirty first of December.
That sounds like paperwork.
It is not. It is counting.
The letter does not go to where a person is.
It goes to the last address the office holds.
Think about who that catches. Somebody who moved.
Somebody in and out of hospital.
Somebody who went to another town to look after a parent.
That address is not where they are standing.
The letter carries a deadline and the deadline is short.
Miss it and the coverage ends.
Not because anything changed about the person.
Because a form did not come back.
Then the appeal, the new application, and the gap in the middle where the
medication is not covered and somebody pays cash or goes without.
So sending that letter twice as often does not create twice the paperwork.
It creates twice as many chances to fall through.
What decides who loses coverage is not what people assume.
Almost nobody loses it because they stopped qualifying.
They lose it because they qualified and could not prove it inside a window
they never saw. So here is the most useful thing you can do this month.
If anybody in your family is on Medicaid, sit with them and look at the address
on that file.
Ask whether it is the address they actually sleep at.
It takes one telephone call and it is worth more than anything else on this
list.
Number two. How far back the program will pay just got shorter.
Say somebody qualified for Medicaid but had never got around to signing up.
Then something serious happens.
The program could reach backwards and pay the bills from before the application
went in. That window was three months.
It is now one month for adults under sixty five, and two months for everybody
else. That was never built for organized people.
It was built for the man who has a stroke on a Tuesday and cannot fill in a
form for two weeks. For the family in a corridor being told their mother is
not coming home, working out the paperwork afterwards because there was no
afterwards to plan in. Three months was the room left for the fact that a bad
night does not wait for your forms to be in order.
One month is a great deal less room, and the people who need it are the very
people least able to move fast inside it.
Anybody well enough to apply on time was never going to need it.
Number three. There is a second door, and it is being held shut behind the
first one. From the thirty first of December there is a new rule for adults
on Medicaid aged nineteen to sixty four.
Eighty hours a month. Work, study,
training or volunteering, any of those count.
Report it, or claim one of the exemptions, or the coverage stops.
Everybody assumes that somebody who loses that coverage simply buys a private
policy instead. That is the reason the first rule does not frighten anybody.
The help that makes a private policy affordable is closed to them.
If the coverage was lost over the reporting rules, that assistance does not
open. So it is not a gap between two things.
It is a door, and a second door
immediately behind it being held shut by the
same hand, for exactly the people who just walked into the first one.
There are exemptions, and that word carries a great deal.
An exemption is real and written down.
It is also a thing you claim, with documents, inside a window.
Nobody applies it to you because your situation obviously fits.
Almost everybody who loses coverage is somebody who qualified for an exemption
and never knew to ask for it. Number four.
It reaches you through the person looking after you.
That eighty hour rule lands on people aged nineteen to sixty four.
So at seventy one it looks like a problem belonging to somebody else entirely,
and that is precisely why it is on this list.
There are three ways it walks into an ordinary older household, and every one
of them is common. The first runs through a grown son or daughter.
If you have a son or a daughter in their forties or fifties on Medicaid, this
reaches them directly. And when a person in that position loses coverage, the
cost does not go away. Somebody still pays it.
It lands on the person who will not let them go without, out of an account
that was never built to carry two households.
The second is the person already caring for you.
Say your daughter left work to look after you and went onto Medicaid herself.
She now has to write down hours.
In a month where most of her waking life is spent inside your house.
There is usually an exemption for caregivers.
She has to know it exists, and prove it, in the middle of doing the caring.
The third is the one nobody connects.
A large share of the care that keeps older people in their own homes is paid
for by Medicaid. And that part of the program is the part states are allowed
to cut first when money is short.
You will never get a notice about it.
It arrives as a waiting list that is longer than it was, an agency in your
county trimming hours, a post that does not get filled.
That is the one that changes your options in five years in a way you cannot
see from here. There is a related thing worth one minute, and I am going to
be honest that it has not been settled.
An old budget rule can trigger automatic reductions in what the government
pays doctors and hospitals for treating Medicare patients.
It does not touch your benefit, your premium, or what you are covered for.
What it touches is how many doctors are willing to take new Medicare patients,
and that shows up in country areas first.
It has been postponed every time it has come up before.
Anybody certain either way is guessing in front of you.
The useful thing does not depend on the answer.
Telephone the office of your own doctor, confirm they still take Medicare,
and get the name of one other practice near you that does.
Five minutes, and worth it whether this lands or not.
Number five. There is no longer a national number you can rely on for a care
home. There was a federal rule setting the minimum number of nursing staff
a care home had to have. A floor.
It was being brought in slowly.
It has now been withdrawn, and nothing is allowed to replace it until the first
of October two thousand and thirty four.
Nine years with no floor. There is a real argument on the other side.
Homes in country areas said they could not hire to that standard at any wage.
A rule they could not meet would have closed them.
And a closed care home, in a county with only one, is worse for everybody.
That argument holds. But here is what it means at your kitchen table, and it
is the only part I want you to carry.
The number is gone. So the question is now yours to ask, and it is not a rude
question. Ask how many nursing hours each resident gets per day.
Ask what the staff turnover has been over the last year.
Ask how much agency cover they use, meaning temporary staff who do not know
the residents by name.
Those three answers tell you more about how somebody will be looked after than
the building, the carpet or the dining room ever will.
And the staffing figures a home reports are published, so you can look before
you ever walk in and know whether the answer you are given matches.
Number six. The door that quietly never opened.
Your state runs a program that pays your Medicare premium for you.
Not pays you back. Pays it. So the amount coming out of your payment before
you see it simply stops coming out.
Your deposit is larger every month, for as long as you qualify.
There is more than one level of it, and the upper levels exist for people whose
income was too high for the first.
For years the problem was never whether people qualified.
Almost nobody knew it existed, and the application was a job in itself, so
millions who qualified never enrolled.
So somebody wrote a rule to close that gap.
The office already knows what you receive each month.
So the rule used those figures to pick out the people who qualified and sign
them up, instead of waiting for them to stumble across it.
That rule has been stopped. The number they expect is roughly one million three
hundred thousand people with Medicare, people who genuinely qualify, will now
not be enrolled who otherwise would have been.
Look carefully at what that is, because it is not what people expect.
Nobody is denied. Nobody loses anything they currently have.
The door simply stays shut instead of opening, and there is no notice for it
and no appeal against it, because nothing was refused.
The only way anybody ends up on the right side of it is by applying the old
way, on their own, having somehow found out it exists.
So here is the call.
Telephone your state Medicaid office, or your area agency on aging, and ask
them to check whether you qualify for the programs that help pay Medicare costs.
The income limits are higher than most people assume, because they are tied
to a federal figure that moves every year, and the person who decides is not
you. I want to name the pattern before I finish.
Once you have seen it, you will see it in everything that comes out of Washington.
There are two ways to spend less on a program.
You can take something away from people who have it, which is visible, which
makes the news, and which somebody has to stand up and defend.
Or you can make it slightly harder to get in the first place, which is invisible,
which produces no story at all, and which saves the same money.
Nothing in that second category will ever arrive in your mail.
You cannot send somebody a notice about a benefit they were never told about.
So, six things, and how each one reaches you.
The letter that proves you still qualify now arrives every six months, at whatever
address they last wrote down. How far back the program will pay has shrunk
from three months to one for most people.
The private policy everybody assumes is the fallback is closed to the people
who just lost the first thing.
The eighty hour rule lands on people under sixty five and walks into your house
through your own family. The care home staffing floor is gone for nine years
and the questions are now yours to ask.
And the program that would pay your Medicare premium is still there, but the
rule that was going to come and find you has been switched off.
None of this is advice about your own situation.
Every state writes its own figures and yours will not be the ones spoken here.
One last thing, and hold on to it for the next six months.
Nobody legitimate is going to telephone you about any of this.
A call or a letter may tell you to verify something, or confirm something,
or sign up again, or pay a fee to protect a benefit.
Because of this law, it is a fraud.
Every time, without exception.
Put the telephone down. And if there is somebody in your family on Medicaid
tonight, do not ask them whether their paperwork is in order.
Ask them one thing. What address is on the file.

title: ⚠️The FED Just Issued a WARNING to Every Senior With a Savings Account (Most Never Hear)

segments.text: Nine days ago the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time
in three years.
Your bank has known for nine days.
Go and look at what it is paying you on the money sitting in your savings account.
Then think back to what it was paying you a fortnight ago.
It is the same number. That is not an oversight.
That is the arrangement, and it is the first of five things that moved against
you this month while nobody was required to write to you about any of them.
The fifth one is the one that takes money out of your hand.
It was written in nineteen eighty three, and it has not been touched since.
Number one. The rate that moved is the rate they charge you.
It is not the rate they pay you.
When the Federal Reserve raises rates, two numbers inside your bank are supposed
to move. What you are charged to borrow.
What you are paid to save.
One of them moves within days.
Your credit card, your overdraft, anything with a variable rate on it, all
of that reprices almost immediately and without asking you.
The other one is left alone. There is no law that forces a bank to pass a rate
rise on to a saver. There has never been such a law.
A bank can hold a hundred thousand dollars of your money in an account paying
you almost nothing, lend that same money out at a rate that just went up, and
keep the difference.
Nobody is breaking a rule. They also know who is least likely to leave.
An account opened in nineteen ninety one, by somebody who has banked at the
same branch for thirty years, is the safest money that bank holds.
It is not going anywhere, so it does not have to be paid for.
Most people assume they are simply getting a poor rate.
They are not.
They are getting the rate a bank reserves for people it is confident will never
check.
Ring your own bank and ask them one question.
What is the highest rate you pay on savings today, on any account you offer.
Then ask which account you are actually in.
In a great many cases those are two different accounts at the same bank, under
the same roof, with the same name on the door.
Number two. On the fourteenth of October a number is announced, and people
have already spent it. Your raise for next year is calculated from an inflation
figure the government publishes on the morning of the fourteenth of October.
The raise is announced the same morning.
The estimates in front of us now are three and a half to three point six per
cent. On an average check that is
somewhere near seventy five dollars a month.
That figure is not decided. It is a forecast, produced by people outside the
government, and it has already been revised more than once this year.
The only number that will matter is the one announced on the fourteenth.
Here is what happens in the weeks before it.
People hear seventy five dollars.
They commit it. They agree to a payment plan, take on a repair, tell somebody
they can help. The money is spoken for in September and does not arrive until
January.
Do not commit that raise before the fourteenth.
And after the fourteenth, still do not commit it, because the amount announced
that morning is not the amount that reaches your account.
Number three. In November they announce what they are taking back.
The Medicare premium for next year is not announced in October alongside your
raise. It is announced in November, weeks later, by a different office.
For this year that premium is two hundred and two dollars and ninety cents
a month, and it comes out of the check before the check reaches you.
You have never had to pay it. You have only ever had it removed.
The projection for next year in the official report is two hundred and nine
dollars and fifty cents. Analysts outside that report expect it to land higher
than the projection, somewhere between two hundred and fifteen and two hundred
and nineteen,
because the official projection has come in low more than once in recent years.
Put the two announcements next to each other.
Seventy five dollars arrives in October as a headline.
Somewhere between seven and sixteen dollars
of it is removed in November, quietly,
in a separate notice, by people who are not the people who announced the raise.
The sequence is doing work.
Published on the same morning, a person sees a raise of sixty dollars and treats
it as sixty.
Published four weeks apart, the same person spends seventy five and is short
in January without ever understanding where the gap came from.
Number four. There is a law that is supposed to stop this.
It leaves three groups outside it.
It is called hold harmless, and almost no older person in this country has
heard the phrase.
What it does is this. The rise in your Medicare premium cannot be large enough
to make your January check smaller than your December check.
The premium increase gets cut down to fit whatever raise you were given.
That is a real protection and it has stopped real money from being taken.
Now the part that is never said in the same breath.
Anything else coming out of your check is outside it entirely.
And it does not cover everybody.
Three groups are outside it. If you are new to Medicare this year, you are
not covered. There is no December check to compare against, so there is nothing
to hold you harmless from. If your income is above the threshold and you pay
the higher income-related premium, you are not covered.
The protection is written for people paying the standard amount.
And if your premium is not deducted from your Social Security check, you are
not covered.
A person who pays Medicare by direct bill, or whose premium is handled by their
state, sits outside the protection without being told they do.
That third group is the one that catches people, because nothing about being
moved onto a different payment arrangement arrives with a warning that a protection
has just been switched off. The one thing worth doing is to know which side
of it you are on. Look at your award letter or your online statement and find
whether the premium is being deducted from the check.
If it is, the protection reaches you.
If it is not, plan on the full increase.
Number five. A number from nineteen eighty three decides whether your raise
gets taxed, and it has never moved.
Until nineteen eighty four,
Social Security was not taxed at all.
Then Congress decided it would be, above a certain income, and wrote the line
at twenty five thousand dollars for one person and thirty two thousand for
a married couple.
Those two figures are the same today.
Not similar. The same. They have never been adjusted for inflation, not once
in more than forty years, while every price you pay has moved and every raise
you have been given has moved with it.
Think about what that does over time.
A person who was safely under that line in nineteen ninety is over it now,
on the same standard of living, having done nothing except receive the raises
they were entitled to. The line did not rise to meet them.
They were carried across it. And it means your raise can cost you.
Seventy five dollars a month is nine hundred dollars a year.
For somebody sitting just below twenty five thousand, that raise is what pushes
them above it, and crossing it brings part of a benefit into tax that was not
taxed the year before. The government does not warn anybody that this is about
to happen to them. There is no letter.
You find out when you file.
The figure they measure you against is not the number on your tax return.
It is your other income, plus any tax-free interest you receive, plus half
of your Social Security.
Notice what is in there. Half the benefit, not all of it.
And tax-free interest counts, even though it is tax-free everywhere else.
So if you are anywhere near that line, the figure to work out before January
is not what you earn. It is that total.
A preparer will calculate it in minutes, most at no charge, and knowing it
in October is worth a great deal more than finding it out in April.
Now the line that runs through all five.
Every one of these was published.
The rate decision, the announcement dates, the premium projection, the protection
and its exclusions, the threshold from nineteen eighty three.
All of it is written down and available to anybody.
Not one of them is going to be sent to you.
That is the whole of the difference.
These are systems built to answer a question, and not one of them is built
to ask you whether you knew. One
correction, because the internet is loud this
month. A rate rise is not a crisis and your money is not in danger because
of it. Your deposits are insured exactly as they were a fortnight ago.
Nothing about your Social Security payment changes because the Federal Reserve
met. Anybody telling you the banks are about to fail is selling you something,
and it is usually on the screen next to them.
The damage here is slower than that and much more ordinary.
It is a rate that does not move, a raise that is smaller than the headline,
and a line from nineteen eighty three that nobody redrew.
So. Five things, and who each one is arranged for.
Your bank will not pass the rate rise on and no law requires it to.
The raise is announced on the fourteenth of October and not before.
The premium that reduces it is announced separately in November.
Hold harmless covers Part B only and leaves three groups outside it.
And the tax threshold has sat at twenty five and thirty two thousand since
nineteen eighty three while everything else moved.
This is education, not advice about your own circumstances.
Your figures are yours and a preparer who sees them will tell you more in ten
minutes than I can from here. If there is somebody in your family living on
a fixed amount, they do not need the Federal Reserve explained to them.
They need one question asked out loud before January.
Is your Medicare premium coming out of your check, or are you paying it another
way.

title: 6 Things They Can't Take From You After 65 — Not Even a Debt Collector

segments.text: A letter comes.
It is printed to look as though a court has already decided something about
you, and it has a number along the top, and a date by which you are told to
respond.
Nothing has been decided.
No judge has seen your name. And the thing most people do within a week of
opening that letter is the single act that can hand the sender a power they
did not have when they posted it.
There are six things a collector cannot take from an older person, and almost
nobody is told what they are. The sixth is not a thing at all.
It is a date, and people give it away by being decent.
Number one. The paper that arrives looks like a court order and is not one.
Look at what is printed on it.
Bold type across the top. A reference number.
Words like final notice, or action required,
or a demand that you reply within
ten days. It is designed by people whose work is to make a piece of company
post feel like a summons.
A real court order carries the name of a court.
A real case has a number issued by that court, and it exists because somebody
filed a lawsuit and because you were handed the papers, by a person, at your
door.
If none of that happened to you, then nothing has been decided about you by
anybody.
Hold that next to what actually happens in a kitchen.
An older woman opens an envelope, reads the word final, and telephones the
number on the page inside the hour.
That call is the whole purpose of the design.
The letter did not need to be true.
It needed to be answered.
So before you telephone anybody, find the name of a court printed anywhere
on that page. If there is one, telephone the clerk of that court and ask whether
a case exists in your name. They will tell you, it costs nothing, and it takes
one call. If there is no court named at all, you are holding an advertisement
with a threatening face on it.
Now the opposite case, because getting this backwards is worse than getting
it wrong in the first direction.
If a real lawsuit has been filed, the papers are handed to you and there is
a deadline printed on them to file your answer with the court.
Depending on the state it runs somewhere between fourteen and thirty five days.
Miss it and the court enters what is called a default judgment, which means
the other side wins because nobody spoke.
Understand what that unlocks, because it is the whole of the danger.
A judgment lets them ask a court to garnish wages, to levy a bank account,
to put a lien on property.
Everything I am about to tell you about protected money still holds afterwards,
but it stops being automatic. That is the sentence to carry out of this video.
The protections exist, and in a court they have to be claimed.
Nobody in that room will raise them for you.
A person who stays silent because the envelope frightened them can lose money
that was never reachable, simply because they were not there to say so.
Number two.
A credit card company cannot reach your Social Security.
Neither can a hospital. This is settled and it is not a grey area.
Ordinary commercial debt cannot touch federal benefit money.
That covers credit cards. It covers a hospital bill.
It covers a shop card, an old medical account, and a company that bought your
debt from somebody else for pennies.
The people telephoning about those debts know this.
They knew it before they dialled.
Nothing in the law requires them to say it to you, and saying it would end
the call. There are limits on how they are allowed to behave while they do
it, and almost no older person has been told them.
They cannot telephone you before eight in the morning or after nine at night.
They are presumed to be breaking the law if they ring you about the same debt
more than seven times in seven days.
And they cannot threaten you with arrest, because an unpaid bill is a civil
matter and nobody in this country goes to jail over one.
There is also a document they owe you.
Within five days of first making contact, a collector has to send you a written
notice naming the original creditor, stating the amount, and telling you that
you have thirty days to dispute it.
If you dispute it in writing inside that window, they must stop collecting
until they have sent you verification.
Most people never use that window, because nobody tells them it is open.
The other direction is true as well and you should hear it from me rather than
from them. Debts owed to the government itself are a separate matter.
Back federal taxes. A federal student loan gone into default.
Support ordered by a family court.
Those have their own machinery and their own limits.
Even those are capped. A student loan offset cannot take more than a set share,
and it cannot push a monthly payment below seven hundred and fifty dollars.
Anyone receiving that figure or less is untouched by it entirely.
So the picture is narrower than the one people carry around.
The category doing the telephoning is almost always the category with no power
to collect.
Number three. There is one payment nobody can touch.
Not even the government.
Supplemental Security Income sits outside all of it.
A commercial creditor cannot reach it.
The government cannot reach it either, and that is the part that surprises
people who assume the government can always take what it is owed.
Not for a tax debt. Not for a student loan.
Not for support. It is the one payment in the entire system that is closed
to everybody.
If that is what arrives in your account each month, then the whole of this
video is about a danger that cannot reach you, and the only thing that can
put your money at risk is something you do yourself.
Which brings us to number six, and I will get there.
Number four. If your money comes from any of these four places, it was never
theirs to take. Veterans Affairs disability payments.
Railroad retirement. Civil Service retirement.
Federal Employees Retirement. Four separate systems, four separate offices,
and every one of them protected in the same way.
A person can spend a year frightened of a collector while every dollar arriving
in their account came from a source that collector was never able to reach.
There is machinery behind these four that runs without you.
A bank served with an order has to review the account itself and set aside
the federal benefit money paid in over the preceding sixty days, and that amount
has to stay spendable. Nobody asks you.
Nobody sends you a form. It turns on one condition.
The payment has to arrive straight from the government into the account.
Money that passed through your hands first is outside the rule, so a paper
payment cashed at a counter and paid in afterwards loses it.
Number five. The tools you work with, and the things inside your house, stay
with you. Every state keeps a list of what cannot be taken from a person regardless
of what they owe. Household furniture.
Clothing. In most states a wedding ring.
Cooking equipment. The tools somebody uses to earn a living, whether that is
a set of wrenches, a sewing machine, or a ladder and a bucket.
The amounts differ enormously from one state to the next, so I am not going
to name a figure that is wrong where you live.
Here is what I want you to notice about this one.
Collectors very rarely go after household goods, because the cost of doing
it is greater than anything they would recover.
It almost never happens. But people give things away anyway, out of fear, because
somebody on the telephone let them believe it could.
Before you agree to anything at all, ask for your own state exemption list.
Your state legal aid office keeps it, they give it out free, and reading it
is often the moment a person stops being frightened.
Number six. Most old debt has a date on it, and one dollar can undo that date.
Every state sets a period during which a debt can be taken to court.
Depending on where you live and what kind of debt it is, it runs somewhere
between three and ten years. When that period ends, the debt is called time
barred, and what that means is precise.
They can no longer sue you for it.
Understand exactly what expires, because this is where people get it wrong
in both directions.
The debt does not vanish. The telephone calls do not stop.
What ends is their right to take you to court.
That is the whole of it, and it is still enormous, because court is the only
route to your money. Now the mechanism, and this is the reason this video exists.
In most states, a partial payment on an old debt restarts that clock from the
day you make it. One dollar does it.
A written promise to pay does it.
In some states, simply saying out loud that the debt is yours can do it.
Think about who that catches. Not the person who ignores the letter.
The person who wants to do the right thing.
Somebody in their seventies, who has never missed a payment in their life,
sends twenty five dollars towards a fifteen year old account because it feels
honest. That twenty five dollars can hand back a right to sue that had already
expired.
Texas is the exception worth naming.
Their state law says a payment does not revive a debt that has already run
out of time. If you are anywhere else, assume it does.
So the date you need is the last payment made on that account, and most people
cannot remember it. There is a free way to find it.
Your credit report lists the date of last activity on each account, and you
are entitled to one from each of the three reporting companies at no charge.
Pull it before you speak to anybody, and write that date on the letter itself.
One more thing collectors rely on.
A debt sold on to a buyer often arrives with very little paperwork behind it,
because the file changed hands for pennies and the documents did not always
travel with it. When somebody disputes in writing and asks for verification,
a fair number of those accounts simply go quiet, not because the debt was imaginary,
but because nobody kept the proof.
So the single most dangerous thing in this entire subject is not a collector.
It is a decent instinct, acted on before anybody checked a date.
Three moves, and none of them costs anything.
This is general information rather than advice about your own circumstances,
because state law differs and yours is yours.
First, pay nothing on an old account until the date is established.
The date that matters is the last payment made on it.
Second, write to the collector and require verification of the debt, including
the month the account fell into default.
Written demands leave a record.
Telephone calls do not. Third, your state legal aid office handles this every
day, free, for older people. They will sit with the letter and read it with
you. One warning about the calls themselves.
If somebody telephones saying they are from a law firm and that papers are
being prepared today, ask for the name of the court and the case number, and
say you will telephone the court yourself to confirm.
A real case survives that question.
Almost nothing else does.
So, six things, and who each one is closed to.
The letter in your hand is not a court order unless a court is named on it.
A credit card company or a hospital cannot reach your Social Security, though
the government can for its own debts.
Supplemental Security Income cannot be reached by anybody at all.
Veterans, railroad, civil service and federal retirement money is protected
the same way, and your bank shields two months of it automatically.
Your household goods and the tools you work with are on a protected list your
state publishes. And most old debt eventually runs out of time, unless you
restart the clock by paying a single dollar.
Every one of those has been written down for years.
It works badly for older people only because the side that knows the rules
is the side being paid to telephone, and the side that needs them is handed
a printed page designed to stop them from reading anything else.
If there is somebody in your family who has been getting these letters and
has gone quiet about it, do not ask them how much they owe.
Ask them one thing. Have you paid anything on it recently.

title: ⚠️ Every Senior Must Do This Before October 1 — Most Never Do

segments.text: On the first of October a set of numbers changes, and not one office holding
those numbers is required to write to you before it happens.
You find out in November.
The amount that lands is wrong, or the door you meant to knock on is already
shut, and the person who could have told you in September was never asked to.
Five things move on that one date.
The same single figure decides all five of them, and most people look at that
figure once, decide they are above it, and never speak to anybody again.
Number one. The food help amount changes on the first, and nobody posts you
the new number.
The federal year turns over on the first of October, and the monthly maximums
turn over with it. For one person living alone the ceiling moves from two hundred
and ninety eight dollars to three hundred and six.
For a household of four it moves from nine hundred and ninety four to one thousand
and twenty three. That is not a large rise and I am not going to pretend it
is. Eight dollars a month for one person.
But notice what nobody does with it.
The figure is set in Washington.
The letter, if one comes at all, comes from your own state, and it comes after
the change rather than before it.
So a household that was told last winter it earned too much is judged this
winter against a different ceiling, and nobody in that household knows the
ceiling moved.
People do not reapply because they remember being refused.
They remember the refusal, not the year it happened in.
And a refusal from two years ago is a refusal against numbers that no longer
exist.
If you were turned down before, you were turned down against an older figure.
Telephone your state benefit office and ask what the monthly ceiling is for
the year that begins in October.
The figure from two winters ago is not the figure they are using now.
Number two. If you are between fifty five and sixty four, something was taken
away from you this month. Until now that age band was excused from the work
rules. That exemption has gone.
From the first of October a person in that band has to be working, volunteering
or training for eighty hours a month, and if they are not, the help stops after
three months and cannot start again for three years.
Three months, then three years of nothing.
I am not going to dress that up.
And here is the piece that catches households rather than individuals.
The rule lands on one person, but the money it removes was feeding a house.
A woman of sixty eight with a brother of sixty living under her roof is not
covered by this rule and will still lose money from her kitchen because of
it. Eighty hours a month is under twenty hours a week, and volunteering counts
in most places, and training counts, and so does looking after certain family
members in some states.
Almost nobody is told that. They hear work requirement, they know they cannot
hold a job, and they walk away from money they could still have kept.
If anybody under your roof is between those two ages, the office can list what
counts towards the eighty hours in your state.
That list is longer than people assume.
Number three. Your county opens a door on the first of October, and most people
find it already shut. Nearly every state has some relief on the property tax
for older owners.
Almost none of it arrives on its own.
It is claimed inside a window, and the window is set locally, and the dates
are not the same anywhere.
In California the filing period for the senior relief opens on the first of
October and closes on the tenth of February.
In New Jersey the reimbursement deadline falls on the thirty first of October.
Different states, one month apart, and nothing connects them except that both
open and close while people are thinking about it.
I cannot tell you your own date and I am not going to guess at it.
What I can tell you is that no county in this country telephones an older owner
to say the window is open. The bill arrives on time every year.
The notice about the relief does not arrive at all.
The county assessor holds one piece of information you need.
The filing window for the senior exemption this year.
Four minutes on the telephone and the date is yours.
Number four. The paper that sets the price you pay in January is already inside
your house.
If you are on a health plan, a document had to reach you before the thirtieth
of September setting out what changes in January.
The cost. The list of medicines.
The doctors. It has arrived. It is somewhere in the post from the last two
or three weeks. It does not come from the government.
It comes from the insurance company that runs the plan, and it looks exactly
like the advertising they send you the other eleven months of the year.
Now look at the timing, because the timing is the trap.
The paper is in your house today.
The period when you are allowed to act on it does not open until the fifteenth
of October, and it closes on the seventh of December.
So you are handed the bad news two or three weeks before you are permitted
to do anything about it. Plenty of people read it, feel a flicker of worry,
put it on a pile, and by the middle of October that pile has been cleared.
Find it this week, while the post is still on the table rather than buried
in a drawer. If it has already gone, the plan will send it out a second time.
The document is called the annual notice of change, and they are required to
give it to you. Number five. For thirty days the heating money is yours alone.
On the first of November you are standing in line with everybody.
There is federal money that pays part of a winter heating bill, and the new
year of it opens on the first of October.
For the first thirty days it is open to a narrow group.
People aged sixty and over. People with a disability.
Households with a child under five.
Households already facing disconnection.
Everybody else has to wait until the first of November.
Read that again, because it is the most valuable thing in this video.
If you are over sixty, you have a month of clear ground in front of you, and
on the first of November everybody else steps in behind you.
The money runs from October until the middle of August, or until it is gone,
whichever happens first. In a hard winter it goes first.
And the people who ring in January are asking for whatever is left after a
month of everybody else. Telephone your state energy assistance office and
say you are over sixty and you want to apply for heating help for this winter.
Say those words and they will know exactly which list to put you on.
Now the line that runs through all five of them.
Every one of these is decided by a single figure, and it is the same figure
every time. What came in last month.
That is the line people are asked for, and it is the line that stops them.
They look at it, compare it against something they half remember, decide they
are above it, and never file. And they are wrong far more often than they are
right, because the number they are
comparing against is usually the wrong year,
and because several of these programs do not count everything that arrives.
Some ignore certain payments entirely.
Some allow costs to be taken off before the figure is judged.
The office decides that. You do not.
And a person who decides it for
themselves, at the kitchen table, in advance,
has refused themselves on a rule they have never read.
So the instruction for all five is the same, and it is smaller than people
expect. Do not open with what you earn.
Say that you want to put in an
application, and let the office decide the rest.
Deciding it is the work they are paid for.
It has never been yours.
Before I give you the dates together, one correction, because the internet
is full of it this month. Nothing collapses on the first of October.
The funding was signed on the second of September and runs to the eleventh
of December.
Payments continue.
No deposit stops.
Anybody telling you the country changes overnight on the first is selling you
a fear that was cancelled three weeks ago, and they are usually selling it
alongside something else. The date that actually matters next is the eleventh
of December. Write that one down instead.
So, five things and the dates on them.
The food help ceiling moves on the first of October, and if you were refused
before, you were refused against an older number.
The work rules land on the fifty five to sixty four band on the same day, and
volunteering and training count.
The property tax window in your own county opens or closes around now and no
one will tell you which. The health plan paper is already in your house and
you cannot act on it until the fifteenth of October.
And the heating money belongs to people over sixty alone until the first of
November. None of this is hidden.
It is written down, it is published, and the dates have been fixed for months.
It works badly for people only because every single one of these offices is
built to answer, and not one of them is built to ask.
This is education and not advice about your own circumstances.
Your state sets its own figures and yours may sit higher than the ones above.
If somebody in your family is living on a fixed amount this winter, they do
not need this explained to them.
They need the dates. Give them the first of October and the first of November,
and let them make the two telephone calls themselves.

title: 6 Bills You Don't Have To Pay After 65 (Most Seniors Don't Know)

segments.text: If you are past sixty five, there is a very real chance you paid a bill this
month that the law does not require you to pay.
You paid it last month as well.
And the month before that, and most likely every month for the last several
years. That money is gone. Nobody is holding it for you.
There is no notice coming and no refund waiting, because the offices collecting
it have no legal duty to tell you that you stopped owing it the day you turned
sixty five.
Their job is to collect. Telling you to stop is not part of that job and never
has been.
I want to be blunt about that,
because it is the single most expensive misunderstanding
I see on this channel.
Turning sixty five did not only make you eligible for Medicare.
It moved you into a different category, and several agencies are required to
treat you differently now.
Almost all of them simply wait to be asked, and most people never ask.
Six of them. Number six takes one letter.
Number one is worth roughly two thousand dollars a year and it has a deadline
that almost nobody hears about.
Let us start. Number six. Jury duty.
Every county keeps a list of names, and yours stays on it long after most people
assume it has been taken off. The summons arrives.
You arrange a ride, you move a doctor appointment, you sit in a room for a
day, because you believe you have no choice in the matter.
In most states you do have a choice once you pass a certain age, and that age
is commonly sixty five or seventy.
Some states excuse you permanently once you ask.
Others excuse you for a term of years and then ask again.
A few want a doctor to sign something.
Many want nothing more than your date of birth on a line.
The form is usually printed on the back of the summons itself, in small type,
inside a box most people never turn over to read.
Look for the word exemption or the word excusal.
If it is not printed there, the clerk of court in your county can tell you
in one phone call, and that call takes about four minutes.
None of this is automatic. The county does not check ages and remove people.
The list is the list until somebody asks to come off it.
Number five.
The trash fee on your county bill.
Find the bill your county sends for solid waste, refuse collection, or sanitation.
In many counties there is a reduction for residents past a certain age, and
in a fair number there is a full waiver.
It can run eighty to four hundred dollars a year depending on where you live.
It is almost never printed on the bill itself.
It sits on the county website under
a heading like senior exemption, age exemption,
or hardship relief, and it is claimed by filling in a single page and showing
proof of age and proof of address.
Some counties take it over the counter the same day.
Now the part that stings. Most counties do not backdate it.
You are exempt from the day they process your form and not one day before.
Every month you spend meaning to get around to it is another month you paid
for something you did not owe, and that money is not recoverable.
Number four. Your vehicle inspection.
If your state requires a safety inspection or an emissions test before you
can renew your registration,
check whether you are still required to have one at all.
Many states exempt vehicles past a certain age from emissions testing.
Several exempt drivers who report very low annual mileage.
A number of rural counties are exempt entirely because the testing requirement
was written for metropolitan areas and never applied outside them.
And some states have dropped safety inspections completely in the last few
years while people carried on booking them out of habit.
People keep paying for a test the vehicle no longer needs, because the reminder
still arrives every year. That reminder is generated by a schedule.
No person reviews your file to see whether you fell outside the requirement
two years ago and nobody is going to write and tell you.
Your state motor vehicle department lists every exemption on its own website
under inspection requirements.
Read that list before you pay for the next one, and if your vehicle is on it,
the money stops this year rather than next.
Number three. Your registration and your plate renewal.
This is the one people ask me about most, and I am going to be straight with
you rather than sell you something that does not exist.
There is no state that hands every senior a free vehicle registration.
What exists is narrower than that, and it is still real money every year.
Some states reduce the registration fee once you reach a set birthday.
Some waive it entirely for a disabled veteran, and a number of those states
extend the same waiver to a surviving spouse who never knew to claim it.
Several states offer a reduced or free disability plate or placard, and that
placard can also remove parking charges you are paying now in your own town.
The one almost nobody checks is this.
If there is a second vehicle you no longer drive, sitting in the driveway or
the garage, you can surrender the plate and stop the registration charge on
it entirely.
People keep paying year after year because cancelling sounds like paperwork.
It is one form at the motor vehicle office and it ends the charge that same
day.
I have watched people pay to register a car they have not started in three
years. Not because they wanted to keep it on the road.
Because the renewal notice arrived, and paying it took four minutes, and asking
the question took longer than that.
Number two. The part of your Medicare premium a plan can pay back.
Some Medicare Advantage plans reduce what comes out of your Social Security
deposit for your Part B premium.
The plan covers a portion of that premium and your monthly deposit rises by
that amount. In some counties it is a small amount.
In others it is most of the premium.
I am not going to tell you to take one.
These plans are not offered everywhere,
and a plan that returns part of your
premium may have a shorter list of doctors,
different rules about seeing a specialist, or different costs when you need
a hospital.
That is a comparison you make with your own doctors written down in front of
you. But it is money, it is decided during the enrollment window each fall,
and most people never once look at whether any plan in their own county offers
it. Your state health insurance assistance program will sit down and compare
the plans with you at no charge, and they do not sell anything.
Number one.
Your Part B premium paid for you, even when you are certain you earn too much.
This is the one that costs people the most, and the reason is a single number
repeated everywhere until it becomes the only number anybody remembers.
Your state runs programs that pay your Part B premium.
There are three levels of them, and almost everyone has heard only the first.
For a single person in two thousand and twenty six, the first level stops at
one thousand three hundred and fifty dollars a month of income.
That is the figure people carry in their heads, and it is the figure that makes
them decide they earn too much and never apply.
The second level goes up to one thousand six hundred and sixteen dollars a
month. The third level goes up to one thousand eight hundred and sixteen dollars
a month. For a married couple the third level reaches two thousand four hundred
and fifty five dollars a month.
So a widow bringing in seventeen hundred a month hears the first figure, decides
she is over the line, and keeps paying that premium out of every single deposit
for years.
She was inside the third level the entire time and nobody told her the other
two levels existed.
The resource limit on all three is nine thousand nine hundred and fifty dollars
for one person and fourteen thousand nine hundred and ten for a couple.
Your house is not counted. Your car is not counted.
Now the part with the deadline on it.
That third level is funded in a fixed amount each year, and the states approve
it first come, first served. Priority goes to the people who already had it
the year before. You also have to apply again every single year to keep it.
Miss your application and your place goes to somebody else, and you wait until
the following year to try again.
Medicare states it plainly on its own page.
Even if you do not think you qualify, apply anyway, because several states
do not count certain kinds of income or certain resources at all, which means
the real limit where you live can sit higher than the printed federal one.
There is one more thing attached to all three levels.
Everyone approved also receives help with prescription costs, and no covered
drug costs more than twelve dollars and sixty five cents in two thousand and
twenty six.
Sit with that for a moment. Somebody reading the first figure and walking away
is not only paying a premium they do not owe.
They are also paying full price at the pharmacy counter every month on top
of it, for the same reason, because of the same single number.
And there is no mechanism anywhere that catches this.
The state does not compare your income against the second and third levels
and write to you. Social Security does not flag it.
Your plan does not mention it.
The only event that starts any of it is you picking up a telephone.
I want to put a figure on the delay, because delay is the whole cost here.
The Part B premium comes out of your deposit every month whether you asked
for it or not. A year of not making the call is roughly two thousand dollars,
plus whatever you paid at the pharmacy that you did not have to.
Two years is double. Nobody sends any of it back.
