rules are different in community property states than in the rest of the country.
This is worth one conversation with an estate attorney to make sure your accounts are
set up to capture the full step up, because the wrong titling can cost the
survivor tens of thousands of dollars she never needed to pay.
The third protective move is your pension, if you have one.
Many pensions default to paying a larger check while the worker is alive and then
stopping completely when that person dies.
There is almost always an option to take a somewhat smaller monthly check in exchange
for the pension continuing to pay the surviving spouse for the rest of her life.
That choice is usually locked in at the moment you start drawing the pension, so
it has to be considered before you retire, not after.
If you are already locked into the single life option, a properly sized life insurance
policy can sometimes replace that lost income for the survivor, but that too requires both
spouses to be healthy enough to qualify, which again means now and not later.
And the fourth protective move is the simplest one and the one people forget.
Check the beneficiary designations on every retirement account, every life insurance policy, and every bank
account, and make sure each one names the person you intend, and consider naming a
backup beneficiary as well.
These forms override whatever your will says.
An out of date beneficiary form is one of the most common and most expensive
mistakes in this entire area, and fixing it costs nothing but a few minutes.
Let me tie it together, because the thread running through all of this is the
same one that runs through everything the system does to seniors.
The widow's penalty is not an accident and it is not a secret, it has
been documented for forty years, and yet no one whose job touches your money has
any reason to bring it up before it is too late.
Your bank will not mention it.
Most generic financial advisers will not model it.
The I R S certainly will not warn you.
It simply waits, quietly, for the day the household goes from two people to one,
and then it collects.
But every single one of these traps can be softened or removed entirely with planning
done while both spouses are still here, still well, and still able to act together.
The couples who sit down and do this work protect the one who will be
left behind. The couples who never get around to it leave that person to face
six tax traps alone, in the worst year of her life.
If you are married, the most loving financial thing you can do is to model
what your taxes will look like the year after one of you is gone, and
then take the steps to protect whoever that survivor will be.
Find a fee only fiduciary adviser or an estate planning attorney who understands the widow's
penalty, and bring them these seven points.
I will put all the details and the things to ask about in the description
below. So do one thing for me right now.
Send this to one married couple you care about, while both of them are still
here to do something about it.
Your parents, your sister and her husband, the couple next door, the two people at
church who have been together fifty years and assume the system will treat the survivor
kindly. It will not.
One quiet conversation tonight, between two people who still have time, can save the one
who is left behind tens of thousands of dollars and a cruel surprise in the
hardest year they will ever face.
That is what we are here for.
I will see you in the next one.

title: 7 Bank Account Moves the IRS Is Flagging for Seniors (Most Don't Know)

segments.text: The moment the amount of money in your bank account crosses a
certain line, your bank starts watching you on behalf of the federal
government and it is legally forbidden from telling you it is happening.
There is a dollar figure that triggers an automatic report to a
federal agency most people have never heard of, there is a second
report that has no dollar figure at all and can be filed
on a withdrawal as small as a few hundred dollars, and there
is a brand new reason banks are now pulling seniors into a
back office and freezing their own money for up to fifteen business
days. None of it is explained to you when you open the
account and none of it is on the statement you get in
the mail. Here is the part that catches good people. For almost
everyone watching, the report itself is harmless. It is routine paperwork that
goes nowhere. The thing that destroys retirees is what they do the
moment they find out the rule exists, because the instinct that feels
the safest is the one that can turn your own legal savings
into a federal investigation. What I am going to walk you through
are seven things about your own bank account that the system will
never sit you down and explain. Every one of them is real,
every one of them is happening right now in twenty twenty six,
and the last one is the quiet mistake that costs families more
money than all the others combined and almost nobody sees it coming.
Stay with me to the end because the final move I am
going to give you takes about ten minutes and it protects everything
you have worked your whole life to save. Number one is the
ten thousand dollar rule and you need to understand what it actually
is before you can stop being afraid of it. Under a law
called the Bank Secrecy Act, which has been on the books since
nineteen seventy, every bank and every credit union in this country is
required to file a report any time you deposit or withdraw more
than ten thousand dollars in cash in a single day. That report
is called a currency transaction report and it does not go to
the I R S. It goes to a bureau inside the Treasury
Department called the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. Your bank files it, not
you. You do not sign anything, you do not fill anything out,
and you will probably never know it happened. The bank has fifteen
days to send it in and it keeps a record of it
for five years. This happens millions of times every year and the
overwhelming majority of those reports go absolutely nowhere. Nobody calls you, nobody
knocks on your door, nobody freezes anything. A currency transaction report is
not an accusation and it is not an audit. It is a
piece of routine paperwork. If you sell a car for twelve thousand
dollars in cash and you walk it into the bank and deposit
the whole thing, a report gets filed and nothing happens to you.
I need you to hold on to that fact because the next
thing I am going to tell you is where people walk straight
into a trap. Number two is the single most dangerous mistake a
retiree can make with their own money and it has a name.
When most people hear about the ten thousand dollar rule for the
first time, they think the same thing. They think well I will
just deposit nine thousand, or I will break it up and bring
in a few thousand at a time across the week. That decision
to deliberately keep your deposits under the line is called structuring, and
under federal law, Title thirty one of the United States Code, Section
five three two four, structuring is a felony. Not a fine, not
a warning letter, a federal crime. And here is the cruel part.
The money does not have to be dirty. You do not have
to be hiding anything. If every dollar is clean, legally earned, legally
inherited, legally gifted to you by your own children, and you simply
break it into smaller pieces to avoid the report, you have committed
the offense. The penalty can be up to five years in federal
prison and fines up to two hundred and fifty thousand dollars, and
the government can seize the entire amount through a process that does
not even require them to charge you with a crime. There are
documented cases of small business owners and widows and ordinary retirees who
had their life savings taken by the government even though the money
was completely legal, simply because their deposits looked like a pattern. The
rule that protects you is simple. Deposit your money all at once,
every dollar of it, and keep a record of where it came
from. Never break it up to stay under a number, because the
act of trying to stay under the number is the only thing
that turns honest money into a federal case. Number three is the
report that has no limit at all, and most people have never
heard of it. On top of the ten thousand dollar report there
is a second one called a suspicious activity report, and this one
has no minimum. There is no floor. A bank can file a
suspicious activity report on a transaction of five hundred dollars, two hundred
dollars, any amount, if the behavior looks unusual to the software that
watches every account. And it is a federal crime for a bank
employee to tell you that one has been filed against you. So
you could be flagged this week and have no way of ever
knowing. What sets it off is not the size of the money,
it is a change in your normal pattern. If you have taken
out three hundred dollars a week for fifteen years and you suddenly
ask for eight thousand to pay a contractor, the system flags the
deviation. It does not know you are putting on a new roof.
It does not care. It flags anything that looks different from your
history, anything that looks like the round numbers people use when they
are trying to stay under the line, and any large deposit that
does not match what the bank knows about your income. This is
exactly why you never want to walk in with an unexpected pile
of cash and no explanation. Bring the paperwork that proves where it
came from and the flag quietly resolves itself. Number four is the
newest one and it is the reason you may have heard that
banks are freezing senior accounts. In the last few years, banks and
brokerages have been given the authority to put a temporary hold on
the account of anyone sixty five or older the moment they suspect
that senior is being financially exploited. The hold can last fifteen business
days and it can be extended longer than that. It was written
with good intentions, to stop scammers from draining a grandmother's savings before
anyone notices. But the same rule means that a perfectly clear headed
retiree who walks in to take out twenty thousand dollars to help
a child buy a home can be pulled into a private office,
questioned about who the money is for and whether anyone told them
to make the withdrawal, and made to wait days while the bank
decides whether to release their own money. There is no age at
which the bank stops treating a large withdrawal as a possible scam,
and arguing with the teller does not speed it up. The way
you stay ahead of this is to tell your bank before the
big transaction, not during it. If you know a large withdrawal is
coming, call the branch, let them note it on your account, and
name a trusted contact person the bank is allowed to call. That
one step turns a multi day freeze into a five minute conversation.
Number five is the two hundred and fifty thousand dollar line that
most seniors have never checked, and it is about protection, not punishment.
Every account at every bank is insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance
Corporation, the F D I C, but only up to two hundred
and fifty thousand dollars per depositor, per bank, per ownership category. If
you have three hundred thousand dollars sitting in a single account at
a single bank and that bank fails, fifty thousand dollars of it
is not insured and you can lose it for good. People think
bank failures are something from the history books, but in twenty twenty
three this country had three of the largest bank failures it has
ever seen inside the span of about ten weeks. The depositors who
were under the limit were fully protected. Anyone over the limit was
at risk and only got rescued because of a political decision that
there is no law forcing anyone to repeat. If you are holding
more than two hundred and fifty thousand dollars in one place, you
can spread it across more than one bank, or across different ownership
categories at the same bank, and bring every dollar back under the
umbrella. It costs you nothing and it removes the risk entirely. Number
six is the quiet mistake I promised you, the one that costs
families the most, and it is almost always done out of love.
At some point a well meaning person tells a widow or a
widower that the simple thing to do is add one of the
children to the bank account, so they can help pay the bills
and so the money passes to them easily later. It sounds reasonable.
It is one of the most dangerous things you can do with
your money. The moment you add your son or your daughter as
a joint owner of your account, that money is legally half theirs.
Which means if that child gets divorced, the account can be pulled
into the divorce. If that child is sued, or has a car
accident, or owes back taxes, or files for bankruptcy, a creditor can
come after the money in your account because your child legally owns
part of it. Any one child you add can legally withdraw every
dollar without asking the others, and I have seen that tear families
apart after a parent is gone. It can disrupt your ability to
qualify for Medicaid, it can create gift tax complications, and it can
quietly override everything you wrote in your will, because a joint account
usually passes straight to the surviving owner no matter what your will
says. The thing that was supposed to make life simpler ends up
handing your money to a lawsuit, an ex spouse, or one child
instead of all of them. Number seven is the fix for all
of it, and it is the ten minute move I told you
to wait for. Instead of adding a child as a joint owner,
you ask your bank for something called a payable on death designation,
a P O D. You stay the only owner of the account
for your entire life. Your children have no access and no ownership
while you are alive, so no creditor of theirs can touch it
and no lawsuit can reach it. But the moment you pass away,
the account goes directly to the people you named, immediately, without going
through probate, without a court, and without a lawyer. It does everything
people think a joint account does, with none of the danger. It
is free to set up and it takes one short conversation at
your branch. And while you are having that conversation, fix the amount
too. The honest answer to how much belongs in a normal checking
or savings account is three to six months of your living expenses,
which for most retirees is somewhere between fifteen and twenty five thousand
dollars, and not much more. Everything above that is being watched, it
is barely earning anything, and it is losing ground to inflation every
month. Move the rest, in your own name, into a high yield
savings account that pays around four percent, into Treasury bills or savings
bonds that you can buy directly from the government through a website
called Treasury Direct, or into certificates of deposit spread across several banks
so every dollar stays insured. You keep full control, you keep full
access, and you earn real money on savings that used to just
sit there being watched. Let me bring all seven together, because there
is one thread running through every single one. The ten thousand dollar
report exists and the bank will not explain it. The structuring law
can punish you for trying to be careful. The suspicious activity report
can be filed on any amount and you will never be told.
The bank can freeze your own money for fifteen days in the
name of protecting you. The insurance only covers you up to a
line you have probably never checked. The joint account you set up
out of love can hand your savings to the wrong person. And
the simple fix for most of it is sitting at your bank
waiting for you to ask for it by name. None of this
comes looking for you. The bank does not call you to lower
your risk. The government does not write to tell you how to
keep your money safe. The system is built so that everything stays
exactly where it is, working quietly against you, until the day you
decide to stand up and move first. You now know what the
line is, you know what not to do when you cross it,
and you know the one designation that protects everything. The only thing
left is to make the call. I will put all the form
names, the website, and the details you need in the description below.
So do one thing for me. Send this to one person over
sixty who keeps most of their savings sitting in a single bank
account. Your mother, your father, your sister, your neighbor, the friend from
church who just lost a spouse and is about to add a
child to the account because someone told them it was the easy
thing to do. The odds are very good that at least one
of these seven things is putting their money at risk right now,
and one share from you could save them thousands of dollars and
a freeze they would never even know was coming. That is what
we are here for. I will see you in the next one.

title: 10 Things the IRS Does the Moment You Turn 65 — Most Seniors Have No Idea

segments.text: The day you turn sixty five the I R S changes how
it treats you and almost none of it is in your favour
unless you know exactly what shifted. Your tax code changes. Your deductions
change. Your Medicare situation changes. Your retirement account rules change. And if
you do not adjust to every single one of these changes the
moment they happen you will spend your entire retirement overpaying on things
the government already said you do not owe. Here are ten things
the I R S does the moment you turn sixty five and
what you need to do about each one. Number one, your standard
deduction goes up but nobody tells you by how much. The moment
you turn sixty five the I R S gives you an additional
standard deduction on top of the regular one. For a single person
sixty five or older in twenty twenty six the extra amount is
two thousand dollars. For a married couple where both spouses are sixty
five or older that is one thousand six hundred each, so three
thousand two hundred combined. That means a single senior gets a total
standard deduction of sixteen thousand eight hundred and fifty dollars before the
senior bonus deduction is even added. Most seniors have no idea this
extra amount exists and they are either filing with the wrong number
or paying a preparer who applies it automatically without ever explaining what
it is or why it matters. Number two, the senior bonus deduction
kicks in and this one is brand new. Starting with the twenty
twenty five tax year every person sixty five or older gets an
additional four thousand dollar deduction on top of everything else. For a
married couple both sixty five or older that is eight thousand. This
stacks on the regular standard deduction and the age related extra deduction.
A single senior can now shelter over twenty thousand dollars of income
from federal tax. A married couple over sixty five can shelter close
to thirty six thousand. For anyone whose total income is at or
below those numbers the federal tax bill is zero and yet millions
of people are still having money withheld from their checks every month.
The senior bonus deduction is temporary and runs through twenty twenty eight
so claim it every year while it exists. Number three, the I
R S starts watching your Social Security differently. Before sixty five most
people are still working and Social Security is not in the picture.
After sixty five if you are collecting Social Security the I R
S calculates something called provisional income to determine how much of your
benefit is taxable. If you are single and your provisional income is
under twenty five thousand, none of your Social Security is taxed. Between
twenty five and thirty four thousand up to fifty percent can be
taxed. Above thirty four thousand up to eighty five percent. Many seniors
do not realise that their I R A withdrawals, their pension income,
and even their tax exempt bond interest all count toward provisional income.
One withdrawal that pushes you over a threshold can suddenly make thousands
of dollars of your Social Security taxable when it was not taxable
the year before. Number four, your Health Savings Account becomes a trap.
If you had a Health Savings Account, also called an H S
A, while you were working, the rules change completely at sixty five.
The moment you enrol in any part of Medicare your eligibility to
contribute to an H S A ends. And here is the part
nobody warns you about. If you delay Medicare enrolment past sixty five
and later apply for Social Security, your Medicare Part A is backdated
by up to six months. Any H S A contributions you made
during that backdated period are considered excess contributions and the I R
S charges you a six percent excise tax on them for every
year they sit in the account. People who thought they were being
smart by continuing to contribute to their H S A after sixty
five get hit with a penalty they never saw coming. Number five,
catch up contributions change. If you are still working at sixty five
and contributing to a four oh one k, the I R S
allows you to make catch up contributions above the normal limit. In
twenty twenty six the standard catch up is eight thousand dollars on
top of the regular twenty four thousand five hundred limit. But if
you are between sixty and sixty three there is a super catch
up of eleven thousand two hundred and fifty. After sixty three it
drops back to the regular eight thousand. For I R A accounts
the catch up contribution is one thousand one hundred dollars. The window
between sixty and sixty three is the most valuable catch up period
the I R S offers and most people blow right past it
without maximising their contributions during those years. Number six, Required Minimum Distributions
start creeping toward you. At sixty five you do not have to
take R M Ds yet but the clock is ticking. Under current
law your first Required Minimum Distribution from a traditional I R A
or four oh one k is due the year you turn seventy
three. That sounds far away at sixty five but here is why
it matters now. The years between sixty five and seventy three are
your conversion window. This is the period when your income is typically
lower because you have stopped working but R M Ds have not
started yet. It is the best time to convert traditional I R
A money into a Roth I R A at a lower tax
rate. Once R M Ds begin your income goes up whether you
want it to or not and every dollar of that distribution is
taxed as ordinary income. If you wait until seventy three to think
about this the window has closed. Number seven, the I R S
lets you make Qualified Charitable Distributions starting at seventy and a half.
This one does not kick in at sixty five but you need
to know about it now so you can plan for it. Once
you are seventy and a half you can send up to one
hundred and eight thousand dollars per year directly from your I R
A to a qualified charity. That money never shows up as taxable
income. It counts toward your Required Minimum Distribution. And it reduces your
adjusted gross income which affects everything from your Social Security taxation to
your Medicare premiums to your eligibility for other deductions. If you give
to your church or any charity and you have an I R
A this is the single most tax efficient way to donate once
you reach the age. Plan for it now at sixty five so
you are ready when the time comes. Number eight, Medicare premiums start
coming out of your Social Security and the I R S is
watching the connection. When you enrol in Medicare at sixty five your
Part B premium is deducted directly from your Social Security check. In
twenty twenty six that base premium is two hundred and two dollars
and ninety cents per month. But if your income is above one
hundred and nine thousand for a single filer, Medicare adds the I
R M A A surcharge which can increase your premium by one
thousand to nearly seven thousand dollars per year. And the income they
use is from your tax return two years ago. Your sixty five
year old self is being charged based on what your sixty three
year old self earned. If you retired between those years and your
income dropped you can file form S S A forty four to
get the surcharge removed. Most people pay it for years without knowing
they can appeal. Number nine, the I R S treats your home
sale differently after sixty five but the rule is the same as
it was before. You can exclude up to two hundred and fifty
thousand dollars of capital gains on the sale of your primary home
if you are single, or five hundred thousand if you are married
filing jointly, as long as you lived in the home for at
least two of the last five years. This rule does not change
at sixty five but the reason it matters is that many seniors
are afraid to sell their home because they think they will owe
a massive tax bill on the appreciation. A couple who bought their
home for one hundred thousand and it is now worth five hundred
thousand has a gain of four hundred thousand. As a married couple
they can exclude the entire amount. Their federal tax on that sale
is zero. The fear of a tax bill that does not exist
keeps people trapped in homes that are too big, too expensive, and
too much work to maintain. Number ten, the I R S gives
you one more year than you think. Here is something almost nobody
knows. The I R S considers you to be sixty five on
the day before your sixty fifth birthday. That means if your birthday
is January first of twenty twenty seven, the I R S treats
you as sixty five for the entire twenty twenty six tax year.
You get the extra standard deduction, the senior bonus deduction, and every
other age related benefit for a full year earlier than you expected.
One day can mean thousands of dollars in tax savings. Check your
birth date against the I R S rules because you might already
qualify for benefits you thought were a year away. Every one of
these ten things happens automatically on the I R S side but
none of the benefits are applied automatically on yours. The deductions do
not appear unless you claim them. The withholding does not stop unless
you file the form. The Medicare surcharge does not get removed unless
you appeal it. The conversion window does not stay open forever. The
I R S changes how it treats you the moment you turn
sixty five. Whether those changes cost you money or save you money
depends entirely on whether you know they happened. I will put all
the form numbers and links in the description below. Send this to
someone who is turning sixty five or who already passed it without
knowing any of this. A spouse, a sibling, a friend. Because the
I R S is not going to call them and explain what
changed. That is what this video is for. I will see you
in the next one.

title: SENIORS: STOP PAYING THESE 5 TAXES — You Are Legally Exempt and the IRS Owes You Money (2026)

segments.text: Every year the I R S collects billions of dollars in taxes
from seniors over sixty five that those seniors do not legally owe
and the reason they keep paying is because nobody sat them down
and explained which taxes apply to them and which ones stopped applying
the day they turned sixty five. There are five specific taxes that
millions of seniors are paying right now that they are either fully
exempt from or dramatically overpaying and in most cases the fix takes
one phone call or one form. Tax number one is federal income
tax and this is the one where the most money is being
left on the table. There is a new deduction that went into
effect with the twenty twenty five tax year that most seniors have
never heard of. It is called the senior bonus deduction and it
gives every person sixty five or older an extra four thousand dollars
off their taxable income on top of everything they already get. For
a married couple where both spouses are sixty five or older that
is eight thousand dollars. And that is in addition to the standard
deduction, which for a single person sixty five or older in twenty
twenty six is eighteen thousand two hundred and fifty dollars, and for
a married couple both sixty five or older is thirty thousand and
seven hundred and fifty dollars. Stack all of that together and a
single senior can shelter over twenty two thousand dollars of income from
federal tax. A married couple both over sixty five can shelter nearly
thirty nine thousand. For millions of seniors living on Social Security plus
a modest pension or a small I R A withdrawal, that means
their federal income tax bill is zero. Legitimately zero. And yet many
of them are still having tax withheld from their Social Security check
or their pension every single month out of pure habit because nobody
told them to update their withholding. The fix is to look at
your actual numbers. Add up your total income, subtract your deductions, and
see what you actually owe. If the answer is zero or close
to it, file a new W four P with your pension provider
and a new W four V with Social Security to stop the
withholding. You are not avoiding taxes. You are stopping the government from
holding your money all year and giving it back as a refund
twelve months later. And here is what makes this urgent. The senior
bonus deduction is temporary. It only exists for twenty twenty five through
twenty twenty eight. Four tax years. If Congress does not extend it,
it disappears. So claim it every single year while it is here.
If you use tax software it will apply automatically when you enter
your age. If someone prepares your return, ask them specifically whether they
applied the senior bonus deduction. I will put all the details in
the description. Tax number two is the tax on your Social Security
benefits and this is the one that confuses people the most because
the rules are not straightforward. Whether your Social Security is taxed depends
on something called provisional income. You take your adjusted gross income, add
any tax exempt interest, add half of your Social Security benefit, and
the total determines how much of your Social Security is subject to
tax. If you are single and that number is under twenty five
thousand dollars, zero percent of your Social Security is taxable. Between twenty
five thousand and thirty four thousand, up to fifty percent can be
taxed. Above thirty four thousand, up to eighty five percent can be
taxed. For married couples filing jointly the thresholds are thirty two thousand
and forty four thousand. Now here is the part that actually matters.
Even at the highest level, fifteen percent of your Social Security is
always tax free. Always. And for a huge number of seniors, especially
those whose primary income is Social Security plus a small amount from
other sources, the combination of the standard deduction and the senior bonus
deduction pushes their taxable income so low that their effective tax on
Social Security is zero even though technically a portion of it is
taxable on paper. The mistake most seniors make is not running the
math. They assume Social Security is fully taxed because someone told them
it was, and they let the government withhold tax from their check
every month without checking whether they actually owe anything. The W four
V form controls how much federal tax is withheld from your Social
Security. You can set it to zero if your actual tax liability
is zero. One form. I will put the details in the description.
Tax number three is your state income tax on retirement income and
this is the one that could be worth more than all the
others combined depending on where you live. Right now forty two states
plus Washington D C do not tax Social Security benefits at all.
Only eight states still tax Social Security in twenty twenty six and
those are Colorado, Connecticut, Minnesota, Montana, New Mexico, Rhode Island, Utah, and
Vermont. And even in those eight states most of them exempt Social
Security for seniors below certain income thresholds. But
Social Security is only part of the picture. 13 states have no
state income tax on any retirement income at all, including 401k withdrawals,
IRA distributions, and pension payments. Those states are Alaska, Florida, Illinois, Iowa,
Mississippi, Nevada, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington, and Wyoming.
If you live in one of those states and you are paying
a tax preparer to calculate state income tax on your retirement income,
you are paying for a calculation that equals zero. And here is
what catches people. Some seniors moved to a state years ago and
never checked whether that state taxes their specific type of retirement income.
Others are having state tax withheld from a pension that is being
paid from a different state, and the rules about which state gets
to tax that pension depend on where you live now, not where
you worked. If you have moved since you're retired, or if you
are thinking about moving, check your state's rules. The difference between a
state that taxes your retirement income and one that does not can
be 3000, 5000, even $10 ,000 a year. Tax number four is
the Medicare surcharge, and most seniors do not even realize it is
a tax. It is called IRMAA, the income -related monthly adjustment amount,
and it is an extra charge that gets added to your Medicare
Part B and Part D premiums if your income is above a
certain level. In 2026, the IRMAA thresholds start at $109 ,000 for
a single filer and $218 ,000 for joint filers. The surcharge can
add anywhere from $1 ,148 to $6 ,936 per year on top
of your standard Medicare premiums. Now, here is the trap that hits
retirees the hardest. Medicare uses your tax return from two years ago
to calculate IRMAA. So if you retired in 2024 and your income
drops significantly, Medicare is still looking at your 2024 return when you
were earning a full salary. They see a high income number and
they charge you the surcharge based on money you are no longer
earning. The fix is a form called the SSA 44. It is
a one -page form that lets you tell Social Security that you
have had a life -changing event and retirement is specifically on the
list. You file the form, you show your current income, and they
recalculate your premiums based on what you are actually earning now instead
of what you earned two years ago. I've seen this single form
save people between $1 ,000 and almost $7 ,000 in a single
year. Filing it takes about 15 minutes. Most people do not know
it exists. I will put the details in the Tax number five
is your property tax. And this one is local, not federal. But
for most seniors, it is the single biggest tax bill they pay
every year. And in almost every case, they are paying more than
they have to. Nearly every state in the country offers some form
of property tax relief for homeowners over 65. The names vary by
state. Some call it a senior breaker credit, but the principle is
the same. Once you reach a certain age, typically 65, you can
reduce the taxable value of your home or freeze your tax bill
so it stops climbing, even if your home's market value goes up.
In Texas, the over 65 exemption reduces your taxable home value by
an additional $60 ,000 for school district taxes and freezes your school
tax at the level it was the year you turned 65. That
freeze has no income limit. It applies to every homeowner over 65,
regardless of wealth. In New York, the enhanced STAR exemption and the
new senior property tax exemption that took effect in 2026 can reduce
your school taxes by up to 65 % of your home's assessed
value. In Florida, the additional homestead exemption for seniors can exempt up
to $50 ,000 of assessed value if your household income is under
a certain threshold. The catch is always the same. None of these
are automatic. Your county does not look at your birthday and apply
the discount. You have to file an application. And in many states,
the application has a hard deadline early in the year. Miss the
deadline and you pay full price for another 12 months. One phone
call to your county tax assessor's office is all it takes. Ask
what senior exemptions are available and whether any of them have no
income limit. That single call can be worth $1 ,000 to $5
,000 a year for the rest of your life. Let me bring
all five together. The senior bonus deduction can push your federal tax
to zero. The Social Security tax may not apply to you at
all, depending on your income level. Your state may not tax retirement
income whatsoever. The IRMAA surcharge can be appealed and eliminated with one
form if you have recently retired. And your property tax almost certainly
has a senior exemption or freeze that you have not claimed. Every
one of these is legal. Every one of them is available right
now. And every one of them requires you to take action because
the government does not refund taxes you overpaid out of ignorance. They
do not send you a letter saying you qualify for a lower
rate. They do not adjust your withholding because you turned 65. The
system takes what you give it and it gives back only what
you ask for. I will put every form number, every phone number,
and every link you need in the description below. Send this to
one person over 60 who is still paying taxes they do not
owe. A parent, a sibling, a friend, someone at church. The odds
are very good that at least one of these five taxes is
coming out of their pocket right now for no reason. And one
share from you could put real money back where it belongs. I
will see you in the next one.

title: 5 Scams Targeting Seniors Right Now — How to Spot Every Single One (2026)

segments.text: Last year seniors over sixty lost more than seven point seven
billion dollars to scams.
That number comes directly from the F B I and it was
a thirty seven percent increase over the year before.
The average victim lost over thirty eight thousand dollars and more than
twelve thousand people lost over one hundred thousand each.
These are not careless people.
These are smart, careful people who got hit by scams that are
specifically designed to bypass everything your brain tells you about being safe.
What I am about to walk you through are the five scams
that are draining the most money from seniors right now in twenty
twenty six.
For each one I am going to tell you exactly how it
works, exactly what the scammer says to get you to act, and
the one thing you can do to shut it down immediately.
If you know what to listen for you will never fall for
any of them.
Scam number one is the Social Security impersonation call and it is
the most common scam hitting seniors in twenty twenty six.
Here is exactly how it works.
Your phone rings and the caller I D says Social Security Administration
or it shows a Washington D C area code.
The voice on the other end sounds official and professional and they
tell you one of three things.
Either your Social Security number has been suspended due to suspicious activity,
or there is a warrant out for your arrest connected to your
number, or your benefits are about to be cut off unless you
verify your identity immediately.
They sound urgent.
They sound serious.
They might even give you a badge number or a case number
to make it feel real.
And then they ask you to confirm your Social Security number, or
they ask you to pay a fee to reactivate your account using
a gift card or a wire transfer or cryptocurrency.
Here is what you need to know.
The Social Security Administration will never call you and threaten to suspend
your number.
That is not a thing that exists.
Social Security numbers cannot be suspended.
They will never threaten you with arrest over the phone.
They will never ask you to pay anything using gift cards or
wire transfers or cryptocurrency.
And they will never call you out of the blue and ask
you to confirm your Social Security number because they already have it.
The one rule that kills this scam is simple.
If someone calls you claiming to be from Social Security and asks
for your number or asks for money, hang up.
Do not press any buttons.
Do not say yes or no.
Just hang up.
If you are genuinely worried that something is wrong with your account
call Social Security yourself using the number on their official website.
I will put it in the description.
Scam number two is the grandparent scam and in twenty twenty six
it has become the most dangerous version it has ever been because
of A I voice cloning.
Here is how it works.
You get a phone call and the voice on the other end
sounds exactly like your grandchild.
Not similar.
Exactly like them.
The same pitch, the same way they say grandma or grandpa, the
same little habits in how they speak.
And they are panicking.
They say they have been in a car accident, or they have
been arrested, or they are in the hospital in another city and
they need money right now for bail or for a lawyer or
for medical bills.
They beg you not to tell their parents.
They say they are embarrassed.
They say please just send the money and they will explain everything
later.
And then someone else gets on the phone, someone claiming to be
a lawyer or a bail bondsman or a police officer, and they
give you instructions on where to send the money.
The reason this scam works so well now is that scammers can
clone anyone's voice from as little as three seconds of audio pulled
from a social media video.
A birthday post on Facebook, a clip on Instagram, a video on
Tik Tok.
The F B I confirmed that these tools are free, require no
technical skill, and produce voices that human listeners cannot reliably distinguish
from the real person.
A I voice cloning scams have cost seniors over two point three
billion dollars in twenty twenty six alone.
The one rule that kills this scam is a family safe word.
Pick a word or phrase that only your family knows.
Not a pet's name, not a street you lived on, not anything
someone could find online.
Something random like purple giraffe or Tuesday pancake.
Agree on it at the next family gathering.
If anyone ever calls you claiming to be family and asking for
money, ask them for the safe word.
If they cannot give it to you, hang up and call your
grandchild directly on the number you already have saved in your phone.
Scam number three is the Medicare scam call and it has hit
a record high in twenty twenty six with a twenty two percent
increase in attempts compared to last year.
Here is what they say.
Someone calls and tells you that Medicare is issuing new cards and
you need to provide your Medicare number to receive yours.
Or they say you are owed a refund because of the new
Part D out of pocket cap and they just need your bank
routing number to deposit the money.
Or they offer you a free back brace or knee brace or
diabetic monitor and say Medicare covers it completely but they need your
Medicare number to verify eligibility.
Every one of these is a lie designed to get your Medicare
number.
Once a scammer has your Medicare number they can bill Medicare for
thousands of dollars of equipment and services you never received.
They can open accounts in your name.
They can use your identity to commit medical fraud that shows up
on your health records and can affect your actual care.
The one rule that kills this scam is knowing that Medicare will
never call you first.
Medicare does not make outgoing phone calls to beneficiaries unless you specifically
requested a callback.
They will never call to offer you a new card because Medicare
cards do not expire and there is no new chip card.
They will never ask for your bank routing number over the phone.
And they will never call to sell you equipment.
If someone calls you about Medicare and you did not initiate the
contact, hang up.
Report it by calling one eight hundred Medicare.
I will put the number in the description.
Scam number four is the romance scam and it is the one
that carries the most shame which is exactly why scammers get away
with it.
In the first half of twenty twenty three alone, half of all
people who lost money to romance scams said it started on Facebook.
Not on a dating app.
On Facebook.
A A R P reports that one in six adults over fifty
say they or someone they know has lost money to a romance
scam and the average loss runs into the thousands.
Here is how it works.
Someone sends you a friend request or a message.
Their profile looks real.
They have photos, friends, posts going back months or years.
They start a conversation.
They are kind and attentive and they say all the right things.
Over weeks or months they build a relationship with you.
They call you.
They text you good morning.
They make you feel seen.
And then the ask comes.
They are stuck overseas and need money for a plane ticket.
They have a medical emergency.
Their business deal fell through and they need a short term loan.
They promise to pay you back.
And because you have spent weeks or months feeling genuinely connected to
this person you send the money.
And then they ask for more.
And more.
And eventually they disappear.
In twenty twenty six these scams have become even harder to spot
because scammers are using A I to generate photorealistic profile pictures and
A I chatbots to maintain conversations around the clock so the person
you are talking to may not even be a real human being.
The one rule that kills this scam is this.
If someone you have never met in person asks you for money,
the answer is no.
It does not matter how long you have been talking.
It does not matter how real it feels.
It does not matter what the emergency is.
A real person who cares about you will never ask you to
wire money or send gift cards or buy cryptocurrency for them.
If they ask for money the relationship is the scam.
Scam number five is the tech support scam and it catches people
in the middle of something they are already worried about which is
why it works so well.
Here is how it starts.
A pop up appears on your computer screen that says warning, your
computer has been infected, call this number immediately.
Or you get a phone call from someone claiming to be from
Microsoft or Apple or your internet provider saying they have detected a
virus on your device.
They sound helpful.
They sound like they are trying to protect you.
They ask you to give them remote access to your computer so
they can fix the problem.
Once they are in they can see everything.
Your bank login, your email, your saved passwords, your personal documents.
They install software that gives them permanent access to your machine even
after the call ends.
And then they either steal directly from your accounts or they tell
you they have found a serious problem and it will cost you
three hundred or five hundred dollars to fix.
The one rule that kills this scam is knowing that no legitimate
technology company will ever call you out of the blue to tell
you your computer has a virus.
Microsoft does not do this.
Apple does not do this.
Your internet provider does not do this.
If you see a pop up warning on your screen close the
browser entirely.
Do not call the number on the screen.
If someone calls you claiming to be tech support, hang up.
If you genuinely believe something is wrong with your computer take it
to a local repair shop or call the company directly using the
number on their official website.
Now here is the pattern that ties every one of these scams
together and once you see it you will never miss it again.
Every scam follows the same five steps.
They pretend to be someone you trust, a government agency, a family
member, Medicare, a love interest, a tech company.
They invent a problem or a prize that requires your immediate attention.
They create pressure so you do not have time to think.
They ask you to pay in a way that cannot be reversed,
gift cards, wire transfers, cryptocurrency, or cash handed to a
stranger.
And they tell you not to talk to anyone else about it.
If any interaction you have follows that pattern, stop.
Hang up the phone, close the browser, step away from the computer,
and call someone you trust before you do anything else.
Call your son.
Call your daughter.
Call your neighbour.
Call a friend.
One phone call to someone who is not in the middle of
the situation with you is the single best protection against every scam
that exists.
I will put all the reporting numbers and links in the description
below.
Send this video to one person over sixty that you care about.
A parent, a grandparent, a friend, someone at church.
Because these scams do not target stupid people.
They target people who pick up the phone, who trust the voice
on the other end, who want to help their family, who are
lonely and open to connection.
They target good people.
And the only defense is knowing what to listen for before the
call comes.
One share from you could save someone thirty eight thousand dollars.
I will see you in the next one.

title: PROTECT YOUR HOME BEFORE YOU NEED A NURSING HOME: Or Medicaid Takes Everything (2026 Warning)

segments.text: The house you spent your whole life paying off is the first
thing the government comes for when you need a nursing home and
the worst part is they wait until you are gone before they
send the bill to your family.
There is a federal program called M E R P, the Medicaid
Estate Recovery Program, and it requires every single state in the country
to recover the cost of your long term care from your estate
after you die.
That means if Medicaid paid for your nursing home, and a typical
stay runs between nine thousand and eleven thousand dollars a month in
twenty twenty six, the state adds up every dollar it spent and
files a claim against whatever you left behind.
And the biggest thing you left behind is the house.
The paid off three bedroom house your family thought they were inheriting
becomes the state's reimbursement fund.
This has been the law since nineteen ninety three.
It is not new.
But the reason most families only find out about it after it
is too late is because nobody in the system has any reason
to warn you.
The hospital social worker who helped your mother qualify for Medicaid told
you the house was safe.
The nursing home admissions coordinator said your mother could keep the home
as long as she intended to return.
And both of those statements were technically true while she was alive.
The moment she passed away the rules flipped.
The home became a recoverable asset and the state filed its claim.
What I am going to walk you through is exactly how this
works, exactly who it affects, and four legitimate legal strategies you can
put in place right now to make sure your home passes to
your family and not to the state.
These are real, these are legal, and every single one of them
requires you to act before you need care because once you are
in a nursing home the window has already closed.
The first thing you need to understand is why Medicare does not save you.
Most people assume that because they paid into Medicare their entire working
life, Medicare will cover a nursing home when they need one.
That assumption is wrong.
Medicare covers what is called skilled nursing care, things like physical therapy
after a hip replacement or wound care that needs a registered nurse,
and it covers that for a maximum of one hundred days.
After day one hundred Medicare stops paying entirely.
But eighty five percent of people in nursing homes are not there
for skilled nursing care.
They are there for custodial care, help bathing, help eating, help getting
dressed, help taking their medication, help not wandering outside at three in
the morning because the dementia took the part of the brain that
knows where the front door leads.
Medicare does not pay for custodial care.
Not for one day.
In twenty twenty six the average cost of custodial nursing home care
in this country is between nine thousand and eleven thousand dollars a
month.
In a memory care unit you are closer to eight thousand for
assisted living and significantly more for a full nursing facility.
The median retirement savings for an American sixty five year old is
roughly two hundred and eighty thousand dollars.
That entire nest egg gets burned through in about two and a
half years of nursing home care.
After that the family applies for Medicaid because Medicaid is the only
government program that covers unlimited custodial long term care.
But Medicaid is a poverty program.
To qualify you need to have two thousand dollars or less in countable assets.
Two thousand.
Your savings, your investments, your life insurance cash value, almost everything has
to be spent down to almost nothing before Medicaid steps in.
The one asset that is technically exempt during your lifetime is your
home, as long as you have the legal intent to return.
But that exemption ends the day you die.
The second thing you need to understand is the five year lookback trap.
Some people hear all of this and think the solution is simple,
just give the house to the kids before you need care and
the state cannot touch what you do not own.
The federal government anticipated that move decades ago.
When you apply for Medicaid the state goes through every financial transaction
you made in the prior sixty months.
Five full years of bank statements, real estate transfers, gifts, everything.
If they find that you gave away assets or sold them for
less than fair market value they impose a transfer penalty.
The penalty is calculated by dividing the value of what you gave
away by the average monthly cost of care in your state.
On a three hundred thousand dollar house in a state where nursing
home care costs ten thousand a month that works out to a
thirty month penalty, two and a half years during which you cannot
receive Medicaid.
You need care, you cannot pay for it, and Medicaid will not
cover you because you tried to give the house away too close
to when you needed help.
This is why last minute planning does not work.
The architecture has to be built while you are still healthy, still
walking, still mowing your own lawn.
Every month you wait the five year clock starts that much later.
Now here are the four strategies that actually protect your home.
Each one is real, each one is legal, and each one works
differently depending on your state and your situation.
Strategy number one is the Medicaid Asset Protection Trust, sometimes called a
M A P T.
This is the most powerful tool available to middle class families in
twenty twenty six.
It is an irrevocable trust which means once you transfer your home
into it you no longer legally own it.
You continue living in the house, you continue paying the property taxes,
you continue maintaining it, nothing changes from the outside.
But legally the home belongs to the trust.
Once five years have passed from the date of the transfer the
lookback window has closed and the home is completely invisible to Medicaid.
When you die the state files its M E R P claim
against your estate but the house is not in your estate.
It is in the trust.
The trust distributes the home to your children free and clear.
The cost to set up a properly drafted M A P T
through an elder law attorney runs between three thousand and ten thousand
dollars depending on your state and the complexity of your situation.
On a house worth three hundred thousand dollars or more that is
the best money you will ever spend.
Strategy number two is the caregiver child exception.
This one is written directly into federal Medicaid law and it is
one of the cleanest exemptions that exists.
If an adult child moves into your home, lives there for at
least two continuous years immediately before you enter a nursing home, and
provides care during that time that allowed you to stay home rather
than go into a facility sooner, you can transfer the home to
that child with zero lookback penalty.
The transfer is exempt.
The requirements are strict.
The child must be a biological or adopted child, not a stepchild or grandchild.
The two years must be continuous and immediately before your institutionalization.
And there must be documentation, medical records showing you would have needed
facility care without the child's help, a caregiving log, and ideally an
attorney structuring the transfer.
But done correctly this is a complete escape from both the lookback
penalty and M E R P recovery.
Strategy number three is the ladybird deed, also called an enhanced life estate deed.
This is only available in a handful of states including Florida, Texas,
Michigan, Vermont, and West Virginia.
A ladybird deed lets you retain full control of your home during
your lifetime, you can sell it, you can mortgage it, you can
do whatever you want with it, while automatically transferring the property to
your named beneficiary when you die without going through probate.
Because the home never enters probate many states cannot recover it through
M E R P.
In Florida a ladybird deed is one of the most powerful and
least expensive Medicaid protection tools available.
An attorney can draft one for between four hundred and one thousand dollars.
It does not help you qualify for Medicaid and it does not
protect the home during the lookback period.
But for M E R P recovery after death in the states
that recognise it, it is devastatingly effective.
Strategy number four is for married couples and it is called the
community spouse resource allowance.
When one spouse needs nursing home care and the other does not,
federal law allows the healthy spouse to keep a protected amount of
assets.
In twenty twenty six the maximum community spouse resource allowance is approximately
one hundred and fifty seven thousand dollars in countable assets plus the
home, plus one vehicle, plus various other exempt categories.
The healthy spouse keeps that allowance and continues living in the home.
The home cannot be sold while they are living in it.
In some states including New York and Florida there is also an
aggressive technique called spousal refusal where the healthy spouse formally declines to
make their income and assets available for the institutionalised spouse's care.
This forces Medicaid to evaluate the nursing home spouse based only on
their own resources which can accelerate eligibility significantly.
The state may later attempt to recover from the healthy spouse but
the immediate Medicaid qualification is preserved.
Now here is what I need you to understand about timing.
Every one of these strategies works best when you are healthy.
The M A P T needs five years to clear the lookback.
The caregiver child exception needs two years of documented live in care.
The ladybird deed needs to be recorded before you need Medicaid.
The spousal protections need to be in place before the nursing home admission.
Once the crisis hits, once the fall happens, once the dementia diagnosis
lands, your options shrink dramatically and the cost of whatever protection you
can still get goes up.
The average American over sixty five has a nearly one in three
chance of needing some form of long term care.
The average stay in a nursing home is just over two years.
The average cost over that stay can easily reach two hundred thousand
to three hundred thousand dollars.
And M E R P operates in every single state in the country.
So here is what you do.
Step one, find out how your home is titled right now.
Is it in your name alone, is it joint tenancy, is it
in a trust.
You need to know.
Step two, find an elder law attorney in your state, not a
general attorney, not a tax preparer, an elder law attorney who specialises
in Medicaid planning.
The National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys maintains a directory.
Step three, schedule the consultation.
It will cost you between two hundred and seven hundred and fifty dollars.
That consultation will tell you which of these four strategies fits your
state, your situation, and your family.
Step four, start the clock.
Whatever the attorney recommends, get the paperwork done because every month you
wait is a month the five year window slides further back.
I will put all the details and links in the description below.
Send this to someone in your family who owns their home and
has no plan for this.
A parent, a brother, a sister, someone at church, someone you care about.
Because right now the most common way families find out about M
E R P is from a certified letter that arrives after the
funeral.
By then the house is already on the line.
One share from you changes that.
I will see you in the next one.

title: Ladies Over 60: STOP Paying These 7 Bills — You're Legally Exempt (Most Don't Know)

segments.text: Right now there are at least seven bills that women over the
age of sixty in this country are paying every single month that
they do not have to pay and the reason nobody has told
you about them is because every person whose job it is to
collect that money from you has absolutely no reason to tell you
that you can stop Your county is not going to call you
and say we can lower your property taxes Medicare is not going
to send you a letter explaining that your premium should be zero
The I R S is not going to remind you that a
brand new deduction worth up to six thousand dollars a year just
showed up in the tax code with your name on it And
nobody nobody at all is going to knock on your door and
tell you that the energy bill you have been struggling with every
single winter has a federal program behind it that will pay your
utility company directly on your behalf What I am about to walk
you through is seven bills plus two bonus moves at the end
for the women who are doing this on their own whether you

yourself Every single one of these is real every one of them
is legal and every one of them requires you to ask for

save you from these bills You have to go get what is
yours Seven bills two bonus moves and the very last one is

Bill number one is your property tax and this is the one

program and the senior enhanced S T A R exemption can knock

your tax base when you move And these are just three states
Nearly every state has something Search your county name plus the words

What programs do you have for homeowners over sixty five and which

phone call you will make this year Bill number two is your
Medicare Part B premium and right now that premium is two hundred

M B which stands for Qualified Medicare Beneficiary If you are single

basically everything Medicare asks you to pay out of pocket All of
it covered by the state on your behalf If your income is
a bit higher up to about one thousand six hundred and sixteen
dollars a month there is another program called S L M B
that will still eliminate that two hundred and two dollar monthly charge
entirely The reason millions of women do not have this is because
you have to apply It is not automatic Nobody enrolls you You
have to go to your state Medicaid office or call one eight
hundred Medicare and ask them to help you apply for a Medicare
Savings Program I will put all the numbers and links in the
description below this video Bill number three is your prescription drug costs
and this one is simpler than you think There is a federal
program called Extra Help sometimes called the Low Income Subsidy and if
you qualify for it the most you will ever pay for a
covered medication is about five dollars for a generic or about twelve
dollars and sixty five cents for a brand name drug Compare that
to the fifty or eighty or one hundred dollars a month that
women without this program are spending on a single medication and you
start to see how much money is being left on the table
The income cutoff for Extra Help in twenty twenty six is about
twenty three thousand nine hundred and forty dollars a year for a

And here is a shortcut most people never find out about If
you already got approved for any of the Medicare Savings Programs I
just told you about in bill number two you are automatically enrolled
in Extra Help You do not have to file a separate application
it just kicks in If you have not done either one yet
you can apply through Social Security online or call them directly I
will put the website and the number in the description Bill number
four is your federal income tax and I need you to pay
very close attention here because this one changed recently and it could
mean the difference between owing the I R S money and owing

have been calling the One Big Beautiful Bill and buried inside it

five tax year every single person who is sixty five or older

living on Social Security plus maybe a small pension or some savings

bill all the way to zero The senior bonus deduction is available

dollars and it only starts to shrink above that number But here
is what makes this urgent As the law stands right now this
deduction only exists for twenty twenty five twenty twenty six twenty twenty
seven and twenty twenty eight Four tax years unless Congress extends it
So this is a claim it every single year while it lasts
situation If you use tax software it will ask your age and
apply it If someone else prepares your return you make sure they
applied it Do not leave six thousand dollars sitting there Bill number
five is the tax you are paying on your Social Security benefits
and a lot of women believe Social Security is always taxed and
that is simply not true Whether your Social Security is taxed depends
on something called your provisional income which is your other income plus
half of your Social Security If you are single and that number
comes in under twenty five thousand dollars then zero percent of your
Social Security is taxable None of it And even at the highest
income levels the maximum that can be taxed is eighty five percent
which means at least fifteen percent of your Social Security is always
tax free no matter what Now here is where women get hurt
the most When you first filed for Social Security you may have
filled out a form called the W four V form telling the
government to withhold federal tax from every single monthly check just to
be safe Then a big chunk of that money comes back as
a refund the next year Think about what that means You are
letting the government hold your money for free all year long on
tax you may not even owe The fix is to look at
your real numbers figure out what you actually owe and file a
new W four V to stop or reduce that withholding so it
matches what you will really owe and not a dollar more Bill
number six is your energy bill and this one hits hardest between
November and March when heating costs climb and your income does not
climb with them There is a federal program called L I H
E A P the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program and it
does not give you a coupon or a percentage off your bill
it sends a payment directly to your gas or electric company on
your behalf Income limits vary by state but if you are a

less there is a strong chance you qualify And if you are
sixty or older you get priority access In most states you can
apply a full month before the general public and that matters because
L I H E A P is first come first served once
the money runs out for the year it is gone until the
next cycle There is also a connected program called the Weatherization Assistance
Program that will send someone to your home to seal up drafts
insulate your walls and repair or replace your heating system at no
cost and that permanently lowers your bill going forward To find your
local L I H E A P office you can dial two
one one that is the national social services line and they will
point you exactly where to go Bill number seven is the fee
you pay to have your taxes done Every year millions of women
walk into a storefront tax office or a big name chain and
pay two hundred to four hundred dollars to have a fairly straightforward
retirement tax return prepared And many of those women legally qualify to
have that exact same return done for free by people the I
R S itself has trained and certified There is a program called
T C E Tax Counseling for the Elderly built specifically for people
sixty and older It specializes in exactly the questions retirees have about
pensions and Social Security and retirement account withdrawals The largest provider is
A A R P Tax Aide which runs thousands of sites across
the country and you do not have to be an A A
R P member to use it Its focus is older adults of
modest to moderate income and that phrase matters because it is not
just for the lowest incomes it covers the broad middle too If
your return is straightforward a couple of Social Security checks maybe a

chain three hundred dollars for forty five minutes of data entry when
a free qualified option exists and your age makes you eligible Now
I promised you two bonus moves and I want to be clear
about who these are for The seven bills I just covered apply
broadly to women at every income level These last two are specifically
for the woman who is managing everything on her own and who
may be leaving the most money on the table simply because nobody
ever sat her down and told her Bonus move number one is
S N A P benefits I know some of you just tensed
up because there is a feeling attached to this one that says
I do not need that that is not for me I am
not in that situation And I want to challenge that feeling with
a fact If you are a woman over sixty living alone on
Social Security and your monthly income is under about one thousand seven
hundred and sixty three dollars you likely qualify for S N A
P and it can put between one hundred and two hundred dollars
or more worth of groceries on your table every single month The
program has special rules for people over sixty You do not have
to meet the gross income test that younger people do You only
need to meet the net income test and you can deduct medical
expenses over thirty five dollars a month from your income which means
your actual threshold is higher than you think Every dollar you save
on groceries is a dollar that stays in your pocket for medication
or your electric bill or just having a little breathing room at
the end of the month Smart women use every resource available to
them and this is a resource that exists specifically because the government
knows that seniors on fixed incomes need it There is nothing to
be embarrassed about You paid into this system your entire working life
You can apply at your local S N A P office or
through your state benefits website and I will put the details in
the description Bonus move number two is for every woman who has
lost a husband or an ex husband and does not know that
Social Security owes her money If your spouse or your ex spouse
passed away and they worked and paid into Social Security during their
lifetime you may be entitled to survivor benefits based on their earnings
record and those benefits can be as high as one hundred percent
of what they were receiving depending on when you claim If you
are sixty or older you can file for survivor benefits right now
If you wait until your full retirement age which is sixty seven
for most women born after nineteen sixty you receive the full one
hundred percent of your late spouse's benefit If you claim earlier the
amount is reduced but it is still real money that is sitting
there waiting for you And here is what most women do not
know If you were married to someone for at least ten years
and they passed away you can claim survivor benefits on their record
even if you are divorced even if you remarried after age sixty
The Social Security Administration does not go out of its way to
tell divorced widows about this You have to know it exists and
you have to ask for it Call Social Security and tell them
you want to explore your survivor benefit options If you were married
if you were married and divorced if your ex spouse died and
you did not know this applied to you it is worth one
phone call to find out what you are owed I will put
all the contact information in the description Let me tie all of
this together with the one thing that matters more than any single
bill I just walked you through Every one of these programs exists
right now The property tax relief is on the books in your
county The Medicare Savings Programs are funded and waiting The senior bonus
deduction is in the tax code The energy assistance is there The
free tax help is open The survivor benefits are sitting in the
system But not one of them comes looking for you Not one
of them mails you a check for the bill you should not
have been paying Not one of them rings your phone to say
you qualify The system is built so the money stays where it
is unless you stand up and claim it You now know seven
bills and two bonus moves and you know that knowing is not
enough You have to pick up the phone you have to fill
out the form you have to walk into the office and say
I am here for what is mine So do one more thing
for me Send this video to one woman in your life who
is over sixty or getting close Your mother your sister your best
friend your neighbor the woman at church who you know is out
here figuring it out by herself The chances are very high that

That is what we are here for I will see you in

title: POV: She Left You for Your Best Friend — 10 Years Later, They Both Found Out What You Built

segments.text: There's a white SUV parked in your spot.
You know it before you even pull into
the driveway. Jake Holloway's SUV. Your
best friend since the ninth grade. The
guy who stood next to you at your
wedding. You're holding a grocery bag
with a box of candles and a little
chocolate cake inside. It's your
daughter's seventh birthday tomorrow.
You left work early so you could hang
streamers tonight. Lauren is standing on
the porch with two packed bags at her
feet. Jake is behind her spinning his
key ring around one finger. He looks at
the gutter, a mailbox, anything except
you. Lauren looks at the grocery bag.
Then she looks at your work shirt, the
one with the apartment company's logo
and a coffee stain on the pocket. You
fix things that belong to other people,
she says, not angry, almost tired. Jake
owns things. A decade from now, the two
of them will be sitting across a
conference table from you, staring at a
contract with your signature on it, and
neither of them will have a single thing
to say. But right now, you just stand on

college 4 years ago. As far as your dad
knows, you mow lawns, do some odd jobs,
and mess around with computers.
You drive a 12-year-old pickup truck.
You rent a small one-bedroom apartment
above a hardware store.
Your dad has worked at the same
packaging plant for 29 years. He
believes in steady paychecks, pensions,
and showing up early. He loves you, and
he is worried sick about you.
What he doesn't know is that you own
five companies. A landscaping company
with 60 employees, a laundry service at
three universities, a vending machine
route with over 400 machines, a moving
company with 18 trucks, and a software
company that over 2,000 businesses pay
every month. Together, they bring in
more than $14 million a year. You're
worth about 9 million. Nobody knows. Not
your dad, not your mom, not your best
friend, not a single person you grew up
with.
You fold the application, put it in your
pocket, and thank your dad. You mean it.
He's trying to help.
Next Saturday, your parents are moving
out of this house. And when the moving
truck pulls into the driveway, your dad
is going to find out everything.
But to understand how you got here, we
have to go back 8 years. To a borrowed
lawnmower, a broken-down old man, and
the best advice you ever got. You're 16.
You want a used car more than anything
in the world. Your parents can't afford
to help, and the grocery store down the
street isn't hiring. So, you borrow your
neighbor's old push mower and knock on
doors.
$20 a lawn.
Most people say no. A few say yes.
One of them is an old man at the end of
your street named Mr. Haskell.
He's 77. He walks with a cane. His lawn
is a jungle because his knees can't
handle the mower anymore.
He sits on his porch with a cup of
coffee and watches you work every
Saturday morning. He never says much.
One day when you finish, he calls you up
to the porch and asks how much you made
that week.
You tell him proudly, "$340."
Then he asks how much you spent.
You think about it. Gas for the mower, a
new pair of sneakers, pizza with your
friends, some video game.
You realize you have about 60 bucks
left.
Mr. Haskell nods slowly. Then he tells
you he was an accountant for 41 years.
He seen doctors go broke and janitors
retire rich, and the difference was
almost never how much they made.
"Most people treat money like a
scoreboard," he says.
"They want everyone to see the number,
but loud money attracts problems. Quiet
money grows."
Then he makes you a deal. Every Saturday
after you mow, you sit on his porch for
30 minutes and he teaches you how to
keep books. In exchange, he'll pay you
double for his lawn.
So, you do. Every Saturday for 2 years,
he teaches you what profit really means,
how to track every dollar, how to price
a job so you don't lose money, how to
save before you spend, not after. By the
end of that first summer, you have 31
regular lawn customers. You've saved
You don't buy the car.
Instead, you buy a second mower and hire
your friend Danny to work with you for
$15 an hour. Then, a used trailer.
By the time you graduate high school,
you have eight part-time workers, 140
customers, and a small landscaping
business that makes more money than your
dad's salary.
And you tell no one.
Because the one time you mentioned it to
a few kids at school, they laughed and
called you the lawn boy for a month. And
one of their parents told your dad that
you were obviously selling something
illegal.
You remember what Mr. Haskell said,
"Quiet money grows."
At 18, you go to the state university,
mostly because your dad wants you to.
He's the first in his family to see a
kid go to college, and he tells everyone
at the plant.
You don't have the heart to tell him
you'd rather keep building.
You hire your friend Danny, the first
guy you ever hired, to run the lawn
business while you're away.
You check the books every Sunday night
from your dorm room.
In your first month of college, you
notice something. Your dorm has 600
students and four washing machines. Two
of them are broken.
Everyone is wearing dirty clothes.
Nobody has time to do laundry.
So, you start a pickup service.
Students drop their dirty laundry in a
bag outside their door. You pick it up,
take it to a laundromat off campus, wash
it, fold it, and bring it back the next
day. $25 a week.
By the end of your first semester, you
have 190 customers.
By the end of your first year, you've
hired eight students to help. By your
second year, you're running the service
at two other universities.
You're barely going to class.
Your grades are sliding.
Your professors don't understand why the
kid in the back row looks so tired.
At 20, you make a decision.
You drop out. Telling your dad is the
hardest conversation of your life.
He sits at the kitchen table in silence
for a long time. Then he says, very
quietly, "I worked double shifts for 20
years so you can have something better
than I had."
You want to explain, but you can already
see how it would sound. A 20-year-old
dropout bragging about a laundry
business. He'd think you were lying, or
worse, being foolish.
So, you just say you're sorry, and that
you have a plan.
He doesn't speak to you for almost 3
weeks.
Your mom tells you later that he went to
the garage every night and just sat in
his truck.

Now, let's see what you built next
