you live. This is the single most common
reason people never apply. They have a
little put aside. They assume it
disqualifies them and they never make
the call. In a growing number of states,
that money is not part of the
conversation at all. Eight, your Part D
plan premium. When you are approved for
one of these programs, something else
happens automatically. You are enrolled
in the Part D drug program called Extra
Help. You do not fill in another form.
You do not make another phone call. It
comes with it. The first thing Extra
Help does is take your Part D plan
premium down to zero up to the standard
plan cost in your area. That used to be
two separate fights. People would win
the premium, then never realize the drug
help was sitting there unclaimed. Now it
follows automatically. If you are
approved, it is yours. Nine. your part D
deductible. The second thing it does is
take your drug deductible to zero as
well. No paying the first few hundred
dollars of your own medicine before the
plan starts helping. The plan helps from
the first prescription of the year. 10.
The price of each prescription. The
third thing is the one you feel every
month. Your cost for each prescription
drops to a small fixed amount instead of
a percentage of the price. For somebody
on four or five regular medicines, that
is not a small saving. That is the
difference between filling everything on
time and deciding which one to skip this
month. I do not need to tell you which
medicine people skip. It is always the
expensive one and it is usually the one
that matters most. Extra help has its
own income limits and they are higher
than the ones for the premium programs.
So there are people who will not get the
premium paid but who will still get
this. It is worth asking about on its
own. Say that clearly to whoever you
speak to. Tell them you want to be
checked for the premium programs and for
extra help. Two checks, one
conversation. If the first one does not
land, the second one still might. 11.
Everything above the yearly drug cap.
This one applies to you whether or not
anything else on this list does. There
is now a yearly limit on what you pay
out of pocket for covered prescription
drugs. This year, that limit is $2,100.
Once you reach it, you pay nothing more
for your covered drugs for the rest of
that year. Nothing. There used to be a
coverage gap in the middle of the year.
People called it the donnut hole. Your
costs would suddenly jump. It does not
work that way anymore. Here is what that
means in practice. Say you take an
expensive medicine. In the old days, the
costs just kept coming month after month
with no end to them. Now they stop. For
somebody with a serious condition, that
is the difference between a bill you can
plan for and a bill with no bottom to
it. 12. Insulin above $35. If you use
insulin, there is a separate protection
on top of everything else. Your cost is
capped at $35 for a month's supply of
each covered insulin. The deductible
does not apply to it either. That cap
holds whether you have any of the help
on this list or none of it. 13. The
yearly visit and the screenings.
Medicare already covers a set of things
at no cost to you with no deductible.
The one condition is that your doctor
accepts Medicare's terms. The yearly
wellness visit is free. So are the
screenings. Cancer screenings, bone
density, diabetes, depression, heart.
The recommended vaccines are free as
well. Flu, pneumonia, shingles, COVID.
If you have been putting one off because
of the price, the price is gone. One
important detail because this catches
people out and leads to a surprise bill.
The free yearly wellness visit is not
the same thing as a full physical
examination. The wellness visit is a
conversation. You go through your
history, your medicines, your risks, and
you build a plan for the year. A full
headtotoe physical is a different
appointment and that one can be build.
So when you book it, use the words. Say
you are booking your Medicare annual
wellness visit. Write them down before
you telephone. Five words and they are
worth money. 14. The help itself. The
last thing you should not be paying for
is somebody to work this out with you.
Every state has a free counseling
service for exactly this. It is called
the state health insurance assistance
program and people shorten it to ship.
It is free. It is onetoone. And the
counselor does not sell insurance and
does not work on commission. They will
sit with you, look at your actual
income, look at your state's actual
rules, and tell you which rung of the
ladder you are on. You can find your
local office online at shiphelp.org, or
ask at your local senior center. You can
also apply directly through your state's
Medicaid office. Before you call, put
four things on the table in front of
you. your Medicare card, your most
recent social security letter, the one
that shows what you are paid each month,
a recent bank statement, and a note of
any other income coming in like a
pension. That is it. No lawyer, no forms
bought from anybody. One phone call and
those four things beside you. And now
the part I want you to hold on to
hardest because where there is money,
there are people who want a piece of it.
Social Security will never ask you to
pay to have your benefits started,
increased, or paid. Nobody legitimate
will ever charge you a fee to apply for
these programs. If somebody telephones
you or knocks at the door and offers to
get your Medicare premium paid for a
fee, that is not a service. Put the
phone down. Here is what all of this
adds up to. On the top level, the state
pays your monthly premium, your yearly
deductible, the 20% share of every bill,
the hospital deductible, and the nursing
facility charge. Your drug costs come
down at the same time. On the second or
third level, the state pays that $22 a
month every month and you keep it. More
than four and 10 people who are entitled
to this are not signed up. Not because
they were refused, because they were
never told, or because they heard the
word Medicaid and decided it was not for
them, or because they looked at one
number, decided they were over the line,
and never asked about their own state.
It costs nothing to ask. It takes one
phone call to a counselor who is paid to
be on your side. Call your local SHIP
office or your state Medicaid office and
ask one question. Ask them whether you
qualify for a Medicare savings program.
That is the whole question, six words.
If the answer comes back no, ask the
second question anyway. Ask about extra
help for your prescriptions. The line
for that one sits higher. And plenty of
people who miss the first still land the
second. And if the answer comes back
yes, tell somebody. Tell your neighbor.
Tell the friend who mentions their
Medicare deduction every month. More
than four in 10 people who are owed this
are not getting it. And the reason is
almost always the same. Nobody told
them. Now you know. So you can be the
one who tells

title: 14 Things They Can't Take After 65 — Not Even the IRS

segments.text: There are 14 things the law says they
cannot take from you after 65, no matter
how much you owe. It covers the income
you live on, the benefits that arrive on
the first, money sitting in certain
accounts, the things inside your house,
and the house itself. That last one is
what people lie awake over, 30 years of
payments, the one thing that was finally
supposed to be finished. And the fear is
always specific. One hospital bill, one
lawsuit, one long stay in a care home,
and it is gone. Here is what they do not
tell you. Against almost everyone who
might come for any of it, the wall is
already built. A credit card company
that sues you and wins still cannot
touch your social security. A collection
agency cannot garnish it. A nursing home
cannot make your benefit its own. Not a
loophole, not a trick. It is written
into federal law in plain words. Your
benefits are not subject to execution,
levy, attachment, garnishment, or other
legal process. And there is an entire
industry that would rather you never
learn that because your fear is the
thing they are selling. But there is a
door in that wall. Congress built the
wall in one law then wrote the key into
a second one. And the second law only
worked because it named the first out
loud. It did. One creditor walks through
that door whenever it chooses. It is not
the hospital. It is not the nursing
home. It is not the collection agency
that has been calling you. And the thing
that most often takes a paid off house
away from someone your age is not even
standing at that door. Two things are
missing from every version of this list
I have seen. The first gets better on
the day you turn 65. Not symbolically,
arithmetically. There is a number and on
your birthday the number goes up. The
second is that door. So, here are all
14. The one worth the most money to you
first. Then I will walk you through it.
One, the part of your income a levy is
not allowed to reach and the extra
amount you get for being 65. When the
IRS levies wages, salary, or other
income, the law does not let it take
everything. A minimum amount is
protected every single pay period. How
much depends on your filing status and
how many dependents you claim. The IRS
publishes the figures in publication
1494. In its own opening line says the
tables show the take-home pay exempt
from a levy in 2026. Here is the part
almost nobody sees. Those tables carry a
separate column headed at least 65 years
old and or blind. These are the IRS's
own worked examples, not mine. A single
taxpayer paid weekly claiming three
dependents has $615.38
protected from the levy. If that same
taxpayer is over 65, it becomes $654.80.
more every week for as long as that levy
runs. married filing jointly, paid every
two weeks, two dependents, $1,64616
is protected. If that taxpayer is over
65 and has a spouse who is blind, it
becomes $1,7738.
Paid monthly, the additional amount is
83 for one and $34167
for two. Here is the sentence worth the
whole video. It is not automatic. Nobody
at the IRS knows how old you are from
the levy paperwork and your employer is
not going to ask. It is yours by law and
it sits unclaimed unless you claim it.
When a levy lands on your wages, your
employer hands you a statement of
dependence and filing status. On parts
three, four, and five of that form,
there is a box labeled additional
standard deduction, and you write a
number in it. The IRS's own instruction
for a taxpayer over 65 whose spouse is
blind is to write two in that space, and
you have 3 days to complete it and
return it. That is the IRS's own word.
Three, miss that window. And here is
what the IRS says happens. Your exempt
amount is figured as if you are married
filing separately with no dependence.
Zero. That is the smallest number in the
entire table. So, the most valuable
thing on this list is a box on a form.
You have 72 hours to return. Count your
additional amounts. Now, you over 65 is
one. You blind is one. Your spouse over
65 is one. Your spouse blind is one. Two
people over 65 in the same house are
counting two. Before I go on, one
practical thing. Because what I just
gave you runs on a clock. You cannot
hold a video open on your kitchen table
while you fill in a form. So I put all
of this into a written guide. every
exemption, the law behind each one, this
year's figures, every deadline plainly
set out, a chapter on the first 72 hours
after a letter arrives, and one on what
to do if you owe and cannot pay. Large
type, and every line names its source,
so you never have to take my word for
anything. Link is in the description and
the pinned comment. If you are watching
on your television, there is a code on
the screen now. Point your phone camera
at it. It is on sale right now. But the
deadline that should actually worry you
is not that one. It is 3 days long and
it starts on a day you do not choose
now. The second one, two, your home and
a federal judge has to sign. Your
principal residence is on the exempt
list. And there is exactly one way it
comes off. The statute says, "A
principal residence shall not be exempt
from levy if a judge or magistrate of a
district court of the United States
approves in writing the levy of such
residence." in writing a federal judge.
The IRS cannot decide on its own to take
your house. It is the strongest line in
the whole section. It protects you from
exactly one opponent and it is not the
one that takes most houses. Three, what
is inside the house? up to $11,980.
Fuel provisions, furniture, and personal
effects in your household. Arms for
personal use, livestock, and poultry. A
lot of people repeat the wrong number
here because the statute still prints an
old figure that was never updated. The
real one resets every year, and for
2026, the revenue procedure puts it at
Four, the tools you work with up to
The books and tools necessary for your
trade, business, or profession. Same
revenue procedure, same year. $5,990.
Five, veterans disability benefits
protected twice over. First, collection.
The statute exempts from levy any amount
payable as a service connected
disability benefit under the listed
chapters of title 38. Second, income.
The IRS says it plainly, "Do not include
disability benefits you receive from the
VA in your gross income. That covers
disability compensation and pension
payments to you or your family, grants
for a wheelchair adapted home, and
grants for a motor vehicle for someone
who has lost their sight or the use of
their limbs. VA education benefits are
excluded, too. So, it cannot be levied,
and it is not income in the first place.
Not much is protected on both ends at
once. Six, workers compensation. Any
amount payable to an individual as
workman's compensation, including any
portion payable for dependence under a
workman's compensation law. That is the
statutory language without
qualification. Seven, supplemental
security income. The statute protects
amounts payable to a recipient of public
assistance under title 4 or title 16 of
the social security act along with state
and local assistance where eligibility
is decided by a needs or income test.
Title 16 is SSI. So SSI is protected
there by name. Title 16. There is
another title. It is not on this list
and that difference matters enormously.
Eight. Railroad retirement and military
retirement annuities. Annuity or pension
payments under the Railroad Retirement
Act, benefits under the Railroad
Unemployment Insurance Act, special
pension payments to someone entered on
the Medal of Honor role, and annuities
based on retired or retainer pay under
chapter 73 of Title 10. Be careful how
far you stretch it. It covers railroad
retirement and certain military retired
pay annuities. It does not cover
ordinary social security retirement and
it does not cover your IRA or your 401k.
I'm coming back to both. Nine,
unemployment benefits. Any amount
payable to an individual with respect to
unemployment, including any portion
payable for dependent under an
unemployment compensation law. The first
nine are what cannot be taken from you.
These five are money the tax code does
not count in the first place. Same
result in your pocket and most lists
blur the two. 10. Life insurance paid
out because somebody died. Generally,
life insurance proceeds you receive as a
beneficiary due to the death of the
insured person are not includable in
gross income, and you do not have to
report them. That is the IRS wording.
Two honest limits. Any interest you
receive on top is taxable and has to be
reported. And where a policy was
transferred to you for consideration,
the exclusion is limited. But the death
benefit itself, the money a surviving
spouse actually lives on, arrives whole.
11. The gain when you sell the home you
live in. $250,000 or $500,000. You can
exclude up to $250,000 of that gain from
your income or up to $500,000 if you
file a joint return with your spouse.
Two tests and you have to pass both. You
or your spouse owned the home for at
least 24 months out of the 5 years
before the sale and used it as a
residence for at least 24 months of
those same 5 years. For a household
selling a house they bought decades ago,
this is often the largest single
exclusion they will ever use. 12. Your
health savings account and what changes
at 65. Money you take out of a health
savings account for qualified medical
expenses is not taxed. You report it on
form 88.889, but you do not pay on it.
Then there is the age line. Take money
out before 65 for something that is not
medical and there is an additional tax
on top of the ordinary income tax. The
IRS says there is no additional tax on
distributions made after the date you
are disabled, reach age 65, or die. So
at 65, that additional tax is gone.
Medical use stays completely tax-free.
Non-medical use is taxed like an
ordinary retirement withdrawal and
nothing worse. So on your 65th birthday,
a health savings account quietly becomes
the most flexible account most people
own. and almost nobody is told. 13. A
qualified Roth distribution and nothing
forcing it out. A qualified distribution
is one made at least 5 years after the
year of your first contribution and made
on or after age 59 a half or on account
of disability or after death. A
qualified distribution is excludable
from gross income. And separately,
unlike a traditional account, nothing
drags the money out on somebody else's
schedule. The IRS answers it directly.
No. If you are the original owner of a
Roth IRA, you do not have to take
distributions regardless of your age.
14. Interest on state and municipal
bonds. Interest on some bonds issued by
a state by the District of Columbia or
by a United States territory to finance
government operations is reportable but
not taxable at the federal level. You
still report it and reporting it changes
nothing. Reporting taxexempt interest is
an information reporting requirement
only and it does not convert it into
taxable interest. And that is the 14.
Now the door. Everything I just gave you
comes out of one section of the Internal
Revenue Code. And that same section has
a sentence near the end that almost
nobody quotes because it does the exact
opposite of everything else in there. It
says that notwithstanding any other law
of the United States, including section
207 of the Social Security Act, no
property or rights to property shall be
exempt from levy other than the property
specifically made exempt. If it is not
on the list, it is reachable. And
Congress went out of its way to name the
Social Security Act specifically, so
nobody could stand up afterwards and
argue otherwise. So here is what they
can take. The first is your social
security check, not SSI. That is title
16. And I told you to hold on to it.
Social Security retirement is title two.
And title 2 is not on the exempt list
anywhere. The IRS runs something called
the federal payment levy program. and
its own page says social security
benefits paid under title 2 federal old
age survivors and disability insurance
benefits will be subject to the 15% levy
through that program 15% of the check
what it does not take SSI under title 16
lumpsum death benefits and benefits paid
to children payments already partly
withheld to repay a debt owed to social
security and disability insurance
benefits because the IRS stopped levying
those systemically on October 5th of
2015. Old age and survivors benefits
carry on at 15%. You may also have heard
that $750 a month is protected no matter
what. That floor is for non-tax debts.
Against the tax debt, the IRS says it
outright. 15% will be levied regardless
of whether or not the remaining benefit
sent to you is less than $750. The
second is your retirement account. When
the IRS sets out what it may seize, it
names them. Wages, retirement accounts,
dividends, bank accounts, licenses,
rental income, the cash loan value of
your life insurance.
An IRA or a 401k is protected from
ordinary creditors in ways it is simply
not protected from the federal
government. Whether a qualified Roth
distribution gets taxed is one question.
Whether the account can be levied is
another. A lot of confident advice
online collapses the two and it is
wrong. The third was in front of us the
whole time. Property tax. Nothing in the
Internal Revenue Code stops your county.
It is a different government and a
different debt. And it is the most
common way an older person actually
loses a home they own outright. That
protection at number two, where a
federal judge has to sign, is a
protection against the IRS. Your county
does not need a federal judge. In 2023,
the Supreme Court decided a case about
exactly this, and it gets reported
backwards constantly. Geraldine Tyler
owned a condominium in Henipin County,
Minnesota. It accumulated about $15,000
in unpaid real estate taxes with
interest and penalties. The county
seized it, sold it for $40,000, and kept
the $25,000 excess over her tax debt for
itself. The court held that the county's
retention of the excess value of her
home above her tax debt violated the
takings clause. The court did not rule
that they cannot take the house. They
can. Unpaid property tax can still cost
you a home you paid off 30 years ago.
What it ruled is that the government
cannot keep the surplus. The equity
above what you actually owed is yours.
States that had been pocketing it were
taking property without just
compensation. If somebody tells you the
Supreme Court stopped them taking houses
over property tax, they read the
headline and not the holding. And if
this has happened in your family, the
surplus is worth putting in front of a
lawyer. The fourth is not a tax at all.
Medicaid estate recovery. Under federal
law, a state must seek recovery from the
estate of a person who was 55 or older
when they received nursing facility
services, home and community based
services, and related hospital and
prescription drug services or at the
state's option, any items or services
under the state plan, not the IRS, not
the county, your state after you die.
There are real protections in that same
law. Recovery may be made only after the
death of the surviving spouse. Only
where there is no surviving child under
21 or blind or permanently and totally
disabled. There are protections for a
sibling with an equity interest who
lived in the home for at least a year
before admission and for an adult child
who provided care and lived there for 2
years before admission. Those exemptions
are federal and they are real and
families miss them constantly because a
letter arrives that sounds final and
nobody reads past the first paragraph.
And one more because it is the complaint
I hear most often. They took my refund.
Often the IRS did not. A separate agency
runs refund offsets. The Department of
Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service
is authorized by Congress to conduct the
Treasury Offset Program, and a federal
refund can be reduced to pay past due
child support, federal agency non-t tax
debts, state income tax obligations, and
certain state unemployment compensation
debt. So, it might be an old student
loan, a state tax bill, a support order,
not a federal tax debt at all. Find out
which agency took it before you argue
with the wrong one. The offset notice
tells you. Now, a warning and it matters
more than anything else I have said
today. There is a whole industry of
people telling you a tax debt can simply
be cancelled. That there is a secret
account tied to your social security
number. That writing that number without
the dashes unlocks something. That there
is an election you can revoke and the
bill goes away. It is false. All of it.
Everything on this list is a narrow
carveout that limits how the government
may collect. Not one of them erases the
debt itself. There is no form, no
filing, no number, and no election that
makes a tax bill disappear. And people
who act on that advice lose money. Some
are prosecuted for it. I gave you all
14, not so you can fight, but so you
know what is already yours and claim it
inside the deadline. That is where the
actual money is. So look at the whole
board one more time. 14 protections that
are real, written down, and largely
unknown to the people they were written
to protect. One of them gets better on
your 65th birthday and sits unclaimed on
a form with a 3-day window. And four
things that can still reach you. Half of
them nothing to do with the IRS at all.
Which is precisely why a list that stops
at the IRS leaves people unprepared.
There is one question I could not answer
today, and I will not pretend otherwise.
Does putting the house into a trust get
you around Medicaid estate recovery? It
depends on your state, on the kind of
trust, and on when it was done. And
anyone giving you a flat yes or no in a
comment is guessing. If that is your
question, say so below and I will do
that work properly. Because nobody sits
you down and teaches you any of this
when you retire. They simply wait to
find out whether you already knew.

title: Seniors Over 50, Sam's Club Owes You These 15 Things

segments.text: Sam's Club will lower the price of your
membership because you are over 50. Aldi
will not do that. Of all the places
somebody your age actually shops, this
is the only one that puts a smaller
number on the card because of your age
alone. It goes first on this list for
one reason, and it is not that it is the
biggest. It is that it is the only one
of the 15 with a deadline attached. The
other 14 will sit there and wait for
you. This one will not. Here they are.
One, the over 50 membership discount.
Start with why that is worth saying out
loud. Costco has no senior membership.
Their own customer service page says it
flatly. Costco does not offer free or
discounted memberships. Gold Star is $65
and executive is 130. And that is the
same price at 25 years old as it is at
75. Aldi does not run one, either. Aldi
told AARP that the company typically
does not offer discounts at all because
the prices are set centrally. There is
no senior day, there is no senior card,
and there is no loyalty program to join.
Sam's Club is the exception. If you are
50 or older and you are joining as a new
member, the first year is $20 on the
club membership or $50 on plus. The
standard prices are 60 and 120. Both of
those went up by $10 in May of this
year. So, anybody quoting you older
numbers is working from last year's
page. You do not need an AARP card. You
verify your age online through a service
called id.me
using a government-issued photo
identification. And you have to join
through that link for it to count. There
is also something on the renewal that
almost nobody mentions. Sam's Club gives
seniors $10 in Sam's Cash when you
renew. It lands on the account within 4
to 6 weeks, and the membership has to
stay active for 12 months afterwards, or
it can be taken back. Now, the three
conditions, because this is where people
get caught out. The first one is harder
than anybody tells you. It is for new
members only, and their own terms say
you do not qualify if you were a Sam's
Club member at any point in the previous
24 months. Not 6 months, two full years.
A lot of people over 60 have let a card
lapse at some point, and if yours ran
out last year, this is not open to you
yet. The second is the one that costs
money. The discount is for the first
year, only the first year. After that,
it renews automatically at whatever the
standard price is at the time. And
today, that is $60 or $120. So, it saves
you money once, and then it quietly puts
itself back without asking your
permission. You can stop that, and here
is exactly how. Sign in at samsclub.com.
Go to account information, and open auto
renew settings, or say it at any club,
Their terms give you one hard deadline

procedure that is not a refund. You have
to produce all of the original
paperwork, the IGI certificate, the GIA
certificate, whichever came with the
stone. You hand that over and what you
receive is not your money. It is a
jewelry credit memo. Then within 48
hours, a Costco graduate gemologist
inspects the stone for authenticity.
Understand what that means practically.
If you have lost the certificate, you
are in difficulty and there is a gap of
a day or two where you have neither the
diamond nor the money, only a piece of
paper. This matters for one situation in
particular and it is a common one.
Somebody dies and the family is going
through what is left and there is a ring
nobody knows what to do with. If it came
from Costco and it is a carrot or more,
find the certificate before you go
anywhere near a returns counter. Three,
gift cards and shop cards non-
returnturnable. Both of them named in
the policy in the same breath as the
gold. Read that carefully because it is
not saying the card stops working. It is
saying the card cannot be handed back
for your money. Once that value is on a
Costco card, it is committed to Costco.
It does not turn back into money in your
bank account. For most people, that is a
small thing. For one situation, it is
not. And it is a situation that arrives
in a lot of families. Somebody stops
driving or stops shopping or moves in
with a daughter three states away or
into care and there is a Costco card in
a drawer with a few hundred of value on
it. Bought at a time when it made
perfect sense and now there is no Costco
in their life at all. That value does
not come back. It has to be spent by
somebody in that shop. So two practical
things. Do not buy them in large amounts
as a store of value because that is not
what they are. And if you are ever
offered a shop card in place of a refund
at a counter, understand that you are
being offered credit rather than money.
If you want the money, say so and say it
before anything is processed because it
is far easier to ask first than to
unwind afterwards. Four, anything
custommade for you. Costco has a special
order kiosk. blinds, shutters, flooring,
countertops, window treatments, things
made to the measurements of your house.
Custommanufactured products from those
programs are non- returnturnable. And
that is not Costco being difficult.
Nobody can resell a blind cut to the
width of your window. But it is a real
reversal of what you have been trained
to expect in that building. You walk in
knowing you can bring anything back. You
sit down with somebody at a kiosk and
the normal rule has quietly stopped
applying. So measure twice. Ask out loud
at that kiosk, "What happens if this is
wrong?" Make them say it. Five, airline
tickets and tickets to live events. Also
on the non- returnturnable list, Costco
travels flights and the warehouse sells
tickets to shows and events and those
items do not come back under the
guarantee. I want to be careful here
because this is the one people get
confused about. Costco travel packages
are booked under their own terms and
those terms are not this list. what the
return policy names as non-
returnturnable is the airline item and
the live performance event item. So a
plane airline ticket or a ticket to a
show is governed by the airline and by
the venue, not by the Costco guarantee.
Whatever the airlines own rules allow
you, you have. Whatever they do not,
Costco is not going to override at a
returns counter. If your health is
uncertain or you are booking around a
hospital appointment or around somebody
else's treatment, that distinction is
the whole thing. It is the difference
between a change of plan and money that
is simply gone. And it is worth asking
at the desk before you pay which of the
two you are buying. A package and a bare
flight look very similar on a screen and
they are not the same purchase. Six.
Cigarettes and alcohol where the law
says no. The policy says cigarettes and
alcohol are non- returnturnable where
prohibited by law. That is a
state-by-state matter, not a Costco
decision. Small item, easy to remember.
If the bottle was wrong or it was a gift
that came back to you, do not assume
that one travels. Seven, electronics, 90
days, not forever. This is the big one,
and it is the one that costs the most
money. The famous no time limit applies
to most of what Costco sells.
Electronics are the exception and the
window is 90 days from the day you
received it. Here is the full list
because people guess at it and guess
wrong. Televisions, projectors,
computers, touchscreen tablets, smart
wearable devices, cameras, drones,
camcorders, MP3 players, cellular
telephones. 90 days on every one of
those. Now, here is why this catches
people over 60 specifically. And it is
not about being slow with technology. It
is about how a fault actually shows up.
You buy the television in October for
the family at Christmas. It works. It is
fine. Then in February, the sound starts
cutting out or it will not hold the
wireless connection anymore. And you
think, well, never mind. It is Costco. I
will take it in. You are past it. The 90
days ran out in January and nobody rang
to tell you. So the rule is simple. On
anything electronic, use it properly in
the first week. All of it. Every input,
every function, the thing you bought it
for. Do not put it in a cupboard for the
grandchildren in December. Eight. Major
appliances on the same 90-day clock.
Same list. And this is the part that
surprises people because an appliance
does not feel like an electronic.
Refrigerators over 10 cubic feet.
freezers, ranges, cooktops, microwaves,
range hoods, dishwashers, water heaters,
washers and dryers. 90 days, all of
them. And an appliance is exactly the
purchase where the fault arrives late, a
washing machine that is not draining
properly, a refrigerator that is not
holding temperature at the back, a water
heater that was never quite right. These
declare themselves in month five, not
month one. After 90 days, you are not
out of options. The manufacturer
warranty on the machine is still
running. And Costco runs a technical
support service for major appliances
bought there, so there is still somebody
to telephone, but be clear about what
has changed. Before 90 days, the
conversation is with Costco, and it ends
with your money back. After 90 days, the
conversation is about repair with the
manufacturer on their timetable. Both
are worth having. They're not the same
thing, and one of them is very much
slower. So on an appliance, run it hard
in the first fortnite. Put a full load
through the washing machine. Put a
thermometer in the refrigerator
overnight and look at it in the morning.
Use the oven for something that matters.
You are not being fussy. You are inside
a window that closes. Nine. The gallon
of cooking oil. Now we leave the policy
and move to the trolley itself. Because
the second half of this list is not
about rules. It is about arithmetic. Oil
does not keep indefinitely once it is
opened. Light, heat, and air work on it,
and it goes off slowly enough that you
do not notice on any given day. It stops
being what you paid for long before it
smells wrong. So, do the division before
you lift it. How long does a bottle of
oil actually last in your kitchen now?
Not in the kitchen you ran in 1985 with
three children in the house. Now, if the
honest answer is a year, then the saving
on that jug is not a saving. You are
buying 11 months of slow decline at a
discount. 10. The warehouse-sized
spices, same arithmetic, worse ratio. A
jar of paprika that size is built for a
restaurant. Ground spices fade. They do
not become unsafe. They become nothing.
And you end up adding more and more of
something that stopped tasting of
anything 18 months ago. The small jar at
the ordinary supermarket costs more per
ounce and is cheaper per meal that
actually tastes of something. That is
the calculation that matters. 11. The
500count bottle of tablets. This one I
want to be exact about because it is
health and I am not going to be loose
with it. Vitamins, pain relief, ant
acids, anything you take from a bottle.
Costco sells them in counts that are
enormous and the price per tablet looks
unbeatable. Here is the Food and Drug
Administration in their own words. An
expiration date reflects, and I am
quoting, the time period during which
the product is known to remain stable,
which means it retains its strength,
quality, and purity when it is stored
according to its labeled storage
conditions. And on what happens after
that, again quoting, if a drug has
degraded, it might not provide the
patient with the intended benefit
because it has a lower strength than
intended. In addition, when a drug
degrades, it may yield toxic compounds
that could cause consumers to experience
unintended side effects. I will be
straight with you about the limits of
that. The FDA does not single out older
people in that guidance. The group they
name as particularly vulnerable is
patients with serious and
life-threatening diseases. But run the
arithmetic yourself. If you take one
tablet a day, 500 tablets is 16 months.
If you take it occasionally, it is
years. Look at the date on the bottle
and ask whether you will genuinely
finish it inside that date. And there is
a second thing on the bottle that
matters as much as the date, which is
the storage line. stored according to
its labeled storage conditions. A
bathroom cabinet above a shower is heat
and damp twice a day for years. That is
the worst place in the house and it is
where almost everybody keeps them. 12.
Fresh produce in family multiples. The
bananas that come as a fixed bunch you
cannot break up. The salad in the sealed
double pack, the berries in the tall
plastic tower. There is nothing wrong
with any of it. It is priced well and it
is usually good quality. It is simply
portioned for a house with four or five
people eating in it. For one person or
two, a great deal of it goes into the
bin. And the part that hurts is that you
do not experience it as waste. You
experience it as a saving at the till
and then a small disappointment in the
vegetable drawer a week later. And the
two never get connected. So connect them
for one month. Notice what you throw
away. That is your real price. 13. Soft
cheese bakery and the party-sized
prepared food. The tray of sandwiches.
The cake built for a gathering. The
wheel of soft cheese, the pie the size
of a dust bin lid. These are celebration
portions and they are excellent when
there is a celebration. The trouble is
they get bought on an ordinary Tuesday
because they are there and because they
are good value for what they are. And
then they sit in a house with two people
in it and a cake with a three-day life
becomes a duty. 14. The second freezer.
This is the one I would most like you to
hear. At some point, the over buying
stops fitting in the kitchen and the
solution presents itself. put a chest
freezer in the garage. Now look at what
has actually happened. You have spent
several hundred and taken on the
electricity to run it every hour of
every day for years in order to store
food you bought because it was cheaper
in bulk. For a large family, that
machine earns its keep. For one or two
people, it is very often a monument. It
runs, it hums, and the things at the
bottom of it are from a Christmas 2
years ago. Before you buy it, open the
one you have. If there are things in
there you cannot identify, the problem
is not that you are short of freezer
space. 15. Anything at all in the 30
days before you have checked the price,
not a product, this one, a habit.
Costco's price adjustment gives you 30
days. If what you bought drops in price
inside that window, you are entitled to
the difference and they will give it to
you. Two things to know. Costco does not
price match against other shops, only
against its own price. And precious
metals are excluded, which brings us
right back to item one. Most people
never check and nobody telephones to
tell you. 30 days is not a long time to
remember something on your own. Now go
back over that list because there is a
shape in it. The first eight are a
policy. The last seven are a kitchen and
they fail in opposite directions. The
policy items catch you because you trust
Costco too much. You have been told all
your life that you can bring anything
back. So you stop reading and then you
buy the one category where that is not
true. The kitchen items catch you
because you trust yourself too much. You
are shopping the way you shopped when
the house was full. That is the real
thing underneath all of this. And I want
to say it plainly because nobody says it
to people your age. You spent 30 years
cooking for a household. You learned to
buy the big one. It was not greed. It
was competence. It was the correct
decision every week for decades. And it
is why there was always enough. The
household changed. The habit did not.
And a warehouse is a building designed
from the floor up to reward the habit
you have and never mention that it has
stopped fitting your life. Nobody at
that door is going to tell you that the
bulk size is wrong for you now. The bulk
size is the entire business. So take one
question in with you, not how much is
this? Ask how long will this take me to
use? That single question sorts almost
this entire list. It is the question a
shop will never ask you and it is the
one that decides whether the membership
is making you money or quietly costing
you. If this was useful, send it to one
person over 65 who still shops for a
houseful. Return policies, product
lists, and prices change and vary by
warehouse and by state. So, check
cost.com or ask at your own membership
desk before you rely on any of this.
This is general consumer information,
not financial, legal, or medical advice.
If you have a question about your own
medicines, ask your pharmacist. And do
not stop or change anything you take
because of a video. This channel has no
affiliation with Costco Wholesale
Corporation.

title: 15 MORE Places Seniors DON'T Know Give BIG Discounts

segments.text: Here's 15 more places that'll give you a
discount just for your age. And almost
none of them are going to tell you it's
there. I've put them in order of what
you actually save. The first few are
worth hundreds of dollars. The last one,
two bucks off a haircut. I'll tell you
which is which as we go. And one thing
covers all 15. You only get it if you
ask. They're standing right there
waiting for a question hardly anybody
ever asks. One, a cruise at a price the
person in the next cabin is not paying.
Three of the major lines run senior
fairs from age 55. Carnival, Royal
Caribbean, and Norwegian. Royal
Caribbean have built it into the booking
screen. When you get to the part where
you enter who is traveling, there is a
link that says apply a promo code in
exclusive rates. Open that. Choose
seniors age 55 and over and the price
changes in front of you. Carnival run a
dedicated fair calendar for 55 and over
so you can see which sailings are
cheapest for your age before you pick a
date. Norwegian do it differently.
Theirs is 5% for members of AARP booked
at least 9 months ahead. Now, let me put
a real number on this rather than a
percentage because percentages on a
cruise are slippery. The saving is
commonly up to $100 per person. For a
couple, that is $200 off a holiday you
were taking anyway. And here is the part
worth knowing about timing. Those senior
fairs appear most often between 60 and
30 days before sailing when the line is
looking at cabins that have not sold. If
you are retired, you are the person who
can book at 30 days notice. Everybody
else is tied to school holidays. That
flexibility is worth more than the
discount. One correction because I have
seen this repeated in other videos and
it is not right. Princess does not run
the 55 and over senior rate. People name
it in these lists and it simply is not
there. Carnival, Royal Caribbean, and
Norwegian. Those three. Two, the hotel
room and the discount most people leave
on the desk. Lita is the one worth
starting with. Through AARP, their
published member rate runs from 10 to
20% off. You will also see it reported
that they take up to 30% off standard
rates for guests 55 and over. I have
seen that figure in a great many places,
and I could not confirm it on Windham's
own pages. So, I am telling you what I
know rather than the biggest number I
could find. Ask for both and take
whichever is larger on the day. Think
about what even 10 or 20% does to a long
drive. 400 miles to see a daughter, one
night on the way in each direction,
twice a year. That adds up quietly. You
have to ask for the senior rate when you
book and take identification because
they will ask at check-in. 3 4 5 6 and 7
the rest of the hotels because the ages
are all different and that is where
people lose money. Windom run a senior
rate from 60. And the useful thing about
Windham is how many roadside names sit
underneath it. Days in Raada, Super 8,
Travel Lodge, Lita as well. So, one age
rule covers most of the places you would
actually stop at on a long drive. Best
Western is up to 10% from 60 or with an
AARP card. Marriott is 62 and over. And
here is the detail that catches people.
Marriott does not take AARP. They run
their own senior rate instead for
anybody 62 or older who can show a
driving license. A lot of people assume
that card gets them into everything. At
Marriott, it does not. And if you hand
it over and they say no, you may walk
away thinking there is no discount at
all. There is. Ask for the senior rate
by name. Motel 6 is 5% at 60. But if you
have AARP, it is 10% plus late checkout
at Motel 6 and Studio 6. That late
checkout is the part nobody ever asks
for. And at our age, an extra two hours
in the morning is worth more than the
5%. And Hilton is 65 and over, up to 7%
off the best available rate, and it
covers your family traveling with you,
not just you. Five chains, five
different ages. 55, 60, 62, 65. There is
no logic to it and nobody publishes a
chart. That is the whole reason people
miss them. Eight. 10% off the car
repair. And this one includes the labor.
Pep Boys give 10% off parts and labor to
anybody 55 and over. You need valid
identification and it is instore only at
participating locations. I want to
underline the word labor because that is
what makes this unusual. Almost every
motor discount you will ever be offered
covers parts and stops there. And on a
modern repair, the labor is most of the
bill. A brake job runs somewhere between
$4 and $600. 10% off the whole of that
is $40 to $60. And it applies to oil
changes, tire rotation, and seasonal
servicing, too. One honest caveat on
this one. Pep Boys have somewhere around
800 to 900 stores across 35 states or
so. And they are thickest in California,
Florida, and Texas. So, if you are in
Rhode Island or Maine, there may not be
one near you. Worth a look before you
count on it. You ask at the service
counter before you authorize the work,
not after. Nine. Free food. And I mean
free, not discounted. This is the senior
farmers market nutrition program and
almost nobody has heard of it. If you
are 60 or over and your income is under
the limit, which is around 185% of the
federal poverty level, you qualify for
vouchers, $50 a year in most states. You
spend them at farmers markets, at
roadside stands, and at farm share
programs. That is $50 of fruit and
vegetables that you do not pay for. Two
things you need to know or you will miss
it. It is income tested. So, this one is
not for everybody and I am not going to
pretend otherwise. And most states open
applications in the spring and then
close the window. So, this is not
something you can do on any given
Tuesday. You apply through your area
agency on aging. And the quickest way to
find yours is to search for the letters
SFMP
followed by the name of your state. And
it works the other way around too, which
is worth knowing if you are already on
something. In a number of states, being
enrolled in SNAP or in the senior food
box program is itself accepted as proof
that you qualify for this. In some
places, SNAP enrollment qualifies you
automatically. So, if you are already
receiving one of those, do not assume
this is another long application. It may
already be settled. 10. Up to 30% off at
Goodwill. Most Goodwill stores run a
senior day, usually from age 55, and the
discount tends to sit somewhere between
10 and 30%. But I have to be straight
with you about how this one works
because it is not one company. Goodwill
is a network of regional charities that
each set their own rules. In the
Southern Piedmont territory, it is 25%
off donated items every Tuesday for 55
and over. In Southwest Florida, it is an
extra 20% on Wednesdays. somewhere else
it will be a different day and a
different number. So this is a telephone
call, not a fact. Ring the shop nearest
you and ask two questions. Do you run a
senior day? And which day is it? And if
the idea of a charity shop is not for
you, I would only say this. The clothes
in there were donated by people in your
own town and a great deal of it has
never been worn. 11. 15% and it starts
at 50. Bells run what they call bells
day every Tuesday. an extra 15% off your
purchase in store if you are 50 years of
age or older. 50. That is the lowest age
threshold in either of these videos and
most people qualify for it a full 15
years before they think to ask. Bells is
a Florida company and the shops are
concentrated across the southeast though
they now run in around 23 states and are
still opening. If you know it as Burks
Outlet, that is the same company
renamed. 12 and 13. the cinema which is
cheaper than you think. AMC give a
senior price from 60 depending on the
film and the time of day it is somewhere
between$1 and $4 off and it applies all
day every day not just on a quiet
afternoon. You choose senior when you
buy online or you say it at the box
office. Regal is also 60 and up to $3
off. Same method. Pick senior when
booking or ask. They may want to see
identification. Now, a dollar or two is
not going to change anybody's life, and
I am not going to dress it up, but I
want to say something about it anyway. A
lot of people over 60 stop going to the
cinema. Not because of the money
particularly. It becomes a thing you
used to do. And the price at the counter
when you have not been for a few years
is genuinely shocking and it makes the
decision for you at the door. Knowing
there is a senior price takes that away.
Go on a Tuesday afternoon when it is
empty. It is warm, it is dark, nobody
hurries you, and for 2 hours you are out
of the house. 14. $2 off the haircut for
the rest of your life. Great clips take
$2 off for anybody 65 or over. There is
no coupon and no card. You tell the
stylist when you sit down. Super cuts
run $2 off for 60 and over at selected
salons. $2 is the smallest number in
this video, but you sit in that chair
every 5 or 6 weeks, which is 9 or 10
times a year for the rest of your life.
Nobody ever asks because $2 feels too
small to mention. It is not too small.
It is just not worth mentioning once,
which is a different thing. 15. 5% at
the supermarket on a Wednesday, and I
have to tell you where. Publix take 5%
off for shoppers 60 and over every
Wednesday. But here is what other videos
will not tell you, and it matters. This
is not a companywide policy. It runs at
selected shops in five states: Alabama,
Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina,
and Tennessee. If you are in Florida or
Virginia and you walk up to a Publix
till on a Wednesday expecting 5% because
somebody on the internet said so, you
are very likely to be told no. So, ring
your own shop first. And if you do have
one that runs it, here is how to make it
worth more than 5%. Publix run buy 1 get
one free offers constantly. Do your
Wednesday shop around whatever is on
that offer and take the 5% off the top
of it. Now you are saving on both. So
that is 15 more. Now, before you go, I
want you to look at this list again
because there is a pattern in it that
costs people more money than any single
discount on it. Look at the ages. 50
gets you bells. 55 gets you Lita, Pep
Boys, Goodwill, and the Cruise Lines. 60
gets you AMC, Regal, Publix, Windham,
Best Western, Motel 6, and Supercuts. 62
gets you Marriott. 65 gets you Hilton
and Great Clips. There is no pattern to
that. No agreement, no standard, no
chart on any wall. Every one of those
companies picked a number and told
almost nobody. And the number most
people have in their head is 65 because
that is when Medicare starts. So they
wait, they get to 65, they start asking,
and they never find out that they could
have been asking since they were 50.
That is 15 years of full price paid by
people who qualified the whole time. If
you have a son or a daughter in their
50s, tell them. They are eligible now
for more of this list than you might
think, and there is no chance whatsoever
that anybody has told them. And then
there is the second thing, which is the
same thing I said last time and will
keep saying. None of these go on by
themselves. Not the hotel rate, not the
10% on the labor, not the $2 off the
haircut. There is no card that flags it,
no notice on the door, and no member of
staff anywhere in this country who is
going to look at you and guess. The
people who get these are not better
informed than you. They are not sharper
and they are not luckier. They are just
the ones who open their mouth at the
counter. So ask. The worst that happens
is somebody says no and you are standing
exactly where you were standing anyway.
Senior discounts vary by location and by
franchise owner, change without notice,
and often exclude alcohol, tobacco,
prescriptions, gift cards, and sale
items. Ring your local store or hotel to
confirm before making a special

title: If You're Over 60, Costco Gives You 15 MORE Things Most Members Never Use

segments.text: A few days ago, I sat here and gave you
15 things your Costco card already
includes that most members never use
once. And the thing I did not expect was
how many of you wrote back to say, "I've
had that card for 11 years and I did not
know about a single one of them." So, I
went back through it properly and it
turns out 15 was not the number. 15 was
what I could fit. Here are 15 more. None
of these were in the first video and
this time I've been stricter with myself
about what counts. Every one of these
either puts money back in your pocket or
gives you something at no charge. Costco
sells a great many things to its
members. That is not what this list is.
This is what the fee you have already
paid actually buys you. Let us start
with the one I am most annoyed I did not
know about. One, 15% off repairing the
car you already own. Not buying a car,
repairing the one sitting on your drive
right now. Costco members get 15% off
parts, service, and accessories at
participating service centers
nationwide. Up to $500 off in a single
visit. Read that again because the
number is not small. $500 per visit. It
covers the things that actually go
wrong. Brakes, transmission, heating,
and cooling, alignments, and there are
three details that make this better than
it first sounds. It applies to any
vehicle in your household. It does not
matter where you bought it, and it is
open to every kind of membership. Gold
Star, Business, Executive, all of them.
Two things to know so it works. It is
participating service centers only and
that is not the Costco tire center. It
is a separate network and you need an
authorization number which you get from
the Costco auto program before you go
and you hand it over with your
membership card when you authorize the
work. So the next time a garage quotes
you $1,100 for breaks, that is a $500
conversation you did not know you could
have. Two, the petrol, which for a lot
of people pays the whole membership
before they buy anything else. Costco
fuel is members only and the saving is
genuine. Depending on where you live, it
typically runs 10 to 30 cents a gallon
under the local average and some
analyses put it 20 to 40 cents below
competing stations. Do that on your own
driving. Two fills a month at 30 cents
off on a 15 gallon tank is over $100 a
year. That is most of the membership fee
back before you have walked through the
door. And something that is coming,
Costco has started opening standalone
petrol stations separate from the
warehouses, members only, with far more
pumps. The first is in Mission Viejo in
California. If it is the queue that has
put you off, watch for those. Three, 10%
back on a new roof, a new furnace, or
new windows. This is the biggest single
number in this video, and almost nobody
knows it exists. Costco runs a home
services program with vetted
contractors, heating and air
conditioning, windows, solar, flooring,
bathroom remodels. When the job is
finished, Costco sends you 10% of the
project value back as a Costco shop
card. Now, think about what those jobs

system is commonly $8 to $12,000. 10% of

as good as cash at any Costco warehouse
or on their website. You can buy your

signing the completion paperwork. And if

your 2% annual reward acrews on that
project, too. So, it stacks on top of
the 10%. But here is the part that
matters more than the money. And I want
to say it plainly, the real problem with
a roof or a furnace at 70 is not the

ring. And you know perfectly well that
some of the people knocking on doors in

person you are older home on a weekday
unsure what the job should cost. Going

after the hearing aid. I covered the

the part that decides whether people go

Costco, the follow-up appointments are

Five, 2% back on your medicines. If you

a 2% cash back reward on what you spend
at their pharmacy. And the detail that

prescription costs and your
over-the-counter medicines, not what
your insurance pays, what you pay. For
somebody managing several long-term
prescriptions, that is a real number by
the end of the year. Two honest limits.
It requires the executive membership,
which is $65 a year extra. And the total
2% reward across everything is capped at
in a 12-month period. It arrives each
February as a certificate on your
renewal notice and you can take it as
cash at the warehouse. Spend it or put
it towards next year's membership. Six,
the medicines for the dog and the cat.
The Costco pharmacy fills prescriptions
for animals as well as people, and the
member prescription program covers pets.
Costco lists savings of up to 80% on
popular medications. Veterinary
medicines are very often the same
compounds as human ones, priced as
though they are something else entirely.
If you have an animal on a long-term
medication, take the prescription to the

regularpriced orders at Shutterfly. Not
5%, 51. It applies automatically at the

push you towards and not for the money.
Most people over 60 have thousands of
photographs on a telephone and almost
nothing on paper. A photograph on a

may be nobody. A printed book on a shelf
does not need a password. Put the
grandchildren in it. Write the names and

Eight, a free room and a free dryer

Stanley Steamer, the carpet and duct
cleaning company. Book three rooms of

Nine, buying the car, not just fixing

other. Buying a car is the transaction
most people over 60 genuinely dread. And
it is not about the money. It is about
the afternoon. Sitting at a desk while

Having the price arranged before you

The rest of the home services list.
Beyond the 10% shop card jobs, the same

heaters, generators, and moving services
at member pricing. Same principle as
before. The value is that somebody else
check them first. 11. The card that pays
you back at the pump. If you carry the

5% back on petrol bought at Costco, 4%
on other petrol and electric vehicle
charging up to $7,000 of combined
spending a year, then 1% after that, 3%
on restaurants and eligible travel, 2%
on everything from Costco. Now, a

2023. It is gone. If you see a list

has not been checked. It does still
carry rental car cover, roadside
assistance, and zero liability for
unauthorized transactions. 12. 25% off
the moving truck. Costco members get 25%
off budget truck rental. I am putting
this here because of who is watching. A
lot of people over 60 are moving or
thinking about it. Downsizing, moving
nearer a daughter, leaving a house with
stairs. A local move on a budget truck
commonly runs under $200 a day. 25% off
that on the two or three days these
things actually take is real. 13. And if

executive members get free delivery and
pickup on pods containers, plus up to
20% off the monthly container hire. That

emptying a house they've lived in for 30

It is the only way it gets done at all.
14. There is a second Costco and your

Hundreds of items the ordinary warehouse
does not carry. Much larger quantities
of food and groceries. A far wider run

Two reasons it matters to somebody our
age. If you are the one who cooks for

make sense. And if the ordinary
warehouse has stopped carrying something
you relied on, this is the first place

discontinued. Look up whether there is

15. The order sheet almost nobody fills
in. At the bakery and the deli counter,
there are paper order sheets for special
orders, custom cakes, deli trays, party
platters. You fill one in at the counter
and collect on the day. Most members

somewhere else entirely and pay three

Costco has said an ordering feature is

at the counter, which is precisely why
so few people know it is there. So that
is 15 more on top of the 15 from last
time. 30 things on one card. And I want
to leave you with what I noticed while I
was putting this list together because
it is the whole point of both videos. Go
back over these. 15% on the brakes, 10%
back on the furnace, 2% on the

free room, a free dryer vent. Not one of
them is stacked on a shelf. Every single
one sits behind a counter or a website
or a telephone number or a form. And a
counter only ever serves the people who
walk up to it. That is why none of it is
advertised. Not because it is a secret,

price label on. So the same instruction
as last time, and it is still the only
one that matters. Go to the membership
desk and say, "Tell me everything my
card covers that I am not using." It is
their job to answer. And it takes about
4 minutes. You have been paying for all
of it for years. Go and use it. Prices,
services, percentages, and included
benefits change and vary by warehouse,
